classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: net_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating
items.description: Net ion-cyclotron heating power is the radio-frequency energy absorbed per unit time by the plasma from a specific launcher, excluding losses outside the plasma.
items.documentation: Net ion-cyclotron heating power is the rate at which radio-frequency waves from a specific launcher transfer energy to the plasma. It includes absorption by all plasma particle populations, not only ions. The absorbed power is defined by $$ P = \int_{V_{\mathrm{pl}}} p_{\mathrm{abs}}\,dV $$ where $P$ is the net absorbed power attributable to the launcher, $V_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the entire plasma volume, $p_{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the local radio-frequency energy-transfer rate per volume summed over all absorbing plasma populations and averaged over a radio-frequency cycle, and $dV$ is a volume element. This quantity applies to one launcher, not a sum over launchers. Unabsorbed wave power and dissipation outside the plasma are excluded. The [launched power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna](name:launched_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) is the forward-minus-reflected power directed into the vessel before plasma absorption; it need not equal the absorbed power defined here. The [total power due to ion-cyclotron heating](name:total_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating) sums launched power over all heating antennas and therefore differs in both absorption scope and launcher aggregation.

items.name: neutral_state_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description: Neutral state momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed flux density of linear momentum carried by a specified neutral state and attributed to pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic drift.
items.documentation: Neutral state momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed flux density of linear momentum carried by a specified neutral state and associated with its pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic drift. The quantity denotes the diamagnetic contribution without selecting a particular flux direction or transported momentum component. The contribution is defined componentwise by: $$ \Pi_{ab,\mathrm{ns}}^{\mathrm{dia}} = \rho_{\mathrm{ns}} v_{a,\mathrm{ns}}^{\mathrm{dia}} u_{b,\mathrm{ns}} $$ where $\Pi_{ab,\mathrm{ns}}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the momentum flux, $a$ is its flux-direction index, $b$ is its transported-momentum index, $\rho_{\mathrm{ns}}$ is neutral-state mass density, $v_{a,\mathrm{ns}}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic drift velocity, and $u_{b,\mathrm{ns}}$ is neutral-state linear flow velocity. This is the neutral-state specialization of [momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift). It excludes contributions attributed to other transport mechanisms and is closely related to [neutral_diamagnetic_momentum_flux](name:neutral_diamagnetic_momentum_flux). Sign convention: Positive when the transported neutral-state momentum crosses the oriented reference surface along its positive flux direction.

items.name: boron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description: Number density of boron ions at the radial location of the internal transport barrier, where suppressed cross-field turbulent transport enables steep impurity density gradients to develop.
items.documentation: Boron density at the internal transport barrier is the local number density of boron ions ($Z = 5$) on the flux surface designated as the internal transport barrier reference location. Unless a charge state is specified separately, this quantity represents the elemental boron ion density summed over all ionization states (B$^{1+}$ through B$^{5+}$), excluding neutral boron atoms. The local particle number density is the zeroth velocity moment of the boron-ion distribution function $f_\mathrm{B}$: $$ n_\mathrm{B}(\rho_\text{ITB}) = \int f_\mathrm{B}(\mathbf{v},\, \rho_\text{ITB})\, d^3v $$ where $\mathbf{v}$ is the particle velocity and $\rho_\text{ITB}$ is the normalized minor radius identifying the ITB flux surface. The ITB is a confined-plasma region where locally reduced cross-field transport coefficients permit steep radial gradients in density and temperature to be sustained; the parent concept is described in [density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier). For the analogous boron density at the innermost confined flux surface, see [boron_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:boron_density_at_magnetic_axis).

items.name: oxygen_density
items.description: Total number density of oxygen atoms and ions across all charge states, from neutral to fully stripped, giving the local oxygen impurity concentration at a point in the plasma.
items.documentation: The local oxygen number density $n_\mathrm{O}$ quantifies the total concentration of oxygen impurity per unit plasma volume, encompassing neutral atomic oxygen and all ionic charge states up to fully stripped O$^{8+}$. Oxygen is a ubiquitous low-Z impurity in fusion devices, entering through wall outgassing and vessel conditioning; it contributes to radiative power losses and dilutes the hydrogenic fuel inventory. The total oxygen density is defined as the sum over all ionization states: $$ n_\mathrm{O} = \sum_{Z=0}^{8} n_{\mathrm{O}^{Z+}} $$ where $n_{\mathrm{O}^{Z+}}$ is the number density of oxygen in charge state $Z^+$, with $Z$ ranging from 0 (neutral) to 8 (fully stripped). The local density is inferred from passive extreme-ultraviolet spectroscopy, charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy, and soft X-ray emission tomography. Spatially averaged forms include [line_averaged_oxygen_density](name:line_averaged_oxygen_density) (chord integral divided by chord length) and [volume_averaged_oxygen_density](name:volume_averaged_oxygen_density) (integral over the plasma volume). The dimensionless oxygen_fraction relates this local density to the electron density as an impurity concentration measure. In well-conditioned fusion plasmas the core oxygen density is a small fraction of the electron density; edge concentrations of $10^{15}$–$10^{17}$ m$^{-3}$ are representative of limiter and divertor configurations.

items.name: parallel_total_ion_energy_convection_velocity
items.description: Effective field-aligned velocity multiplying the energy density summed over all ion species to give their combined parallel convective energy flux.
items.documentation: Field-parallel total-ion energy convection velocity is the effective transport coefficient relating the combined ion population's parallel convective energy flux to its transported energy density in the edge plasma. It is the field-parallel projection of the [total-ion energy convection velocity](name:total_ion_energy_convection_velocity). The defining relation is: $$ Q_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} = \mathcal{W}_i\,v_{i,W,\parallel} $$ where $Q_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the combined ion convective energy flux density along the local magnetic field, $\mathcal{W}_i$ is the combined transported ion energy density, and $v_{i,W,\parallel}$ is this effective convection velocity. The subscript $i$ denotes the combined ion population, $W$ identifies the energy transport channel, and $\parallel$ denotes projection along the local magnetic field. The energy density and convective flux are each summed over all ion species and ionic charge states included in the total-ion energy equation; electron and neutral contributions are excluded. The effective velocity is not a sum of constituent velocities and need not equal the bulk ion flow velocity. Gradient-driven diffusive energy flux is excluded from the defining convective flux. Unlike the [parallel ion energy convection velocity](name:parallel_ion_energy_convection_velocity) for an individual ion population, this coefficient closes the summed ion energy equation. Sign convention: Positive when the convective transport is co-directed with the local magnetic field.

items.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate
items.description: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate labels magnetic surfaces by the square root of their axis-to-boundary toroidal-flux fraction, spanning zero at the magnetic axis to one at the equilibrium boundary.
items.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate The coordinate is defined by $$ \rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}} = \rho_{\mathrm{tor}}/\rho_{\mathrm{tor,b}} $$ where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ is the normalized toroidal flux coordinate, $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal flux coordinate of the selected surface, and $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,b}}$ is the [toroidal flux coordinate at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_plasma_boundary). Both unnormalized coordinates use the same magnetic-axis origin and flux reference. Equivalently, $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}^2 = (\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}-\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}})/(\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,b}}-\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}})$, where $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by the selected surface, and $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}$ and $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,b}}$ are its magnetic-axis and equilibrium-boundary values. On nested closed magnetic surfaces, the nonnegative coordinate is constant on each surface, zero at the magnetic axis, and one at the last closed flux surface used as the boundary. It is a surface label, not a surface average, volume integral, geometric distance, toroidal angle, or vector component. The boundary normalization must be nonzero; the definition does not itself specify a continuation outside the last closed flux surface. Signed line-of-sight variants attach an additional geometric branch sign, while their absolute value retains this normalization. Locus-specific quantities, such as the [coordinate at a constraint position](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_constraint_position), evaluate this same label on the magnetic surface containing the specified position. The [coordinate at the separatrix](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_separatrix) equals one when the separatrix defines the equilibrium boundary.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection
items.description: Velocity characterizing convective momentum transport by neutral particles in a resolved internal quantum state, forming the bulk-flow coefficient in the neutral internal-state momentum flux equation.
items.documentation: The neutral internal-state momentum convection velocity is the fluid velocity at which momentum is transported by bulk convective flow in a neutral particle population that is resolved by internal quantum state (such as a vibrational, rotational, or electronic level). It enters the neutral momentum transport equation as the convective coefficient of the state-resolved momentum flux: $$ \Pi_{\rm conv,s} = m_n n_s v_{\rm conv,s} $$ where $m_n$ is the neutral particle mass, $n_s$ is the number density of internal state $s$, and $v_{\rm conv,s}$ is this convection velocity for state $s$. This is the neutral-species-specific form of the internal-state momentum convection velocity, enabling state-resolved neutral momentum transport to be tracked separately from ionic or electron channels. Its effective counterpart, [effective_neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection), incorporates transport contributions beyond simple bulk advection that enter the convective momentum channel. For comparison, neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_convection describes the corresponding convective velocity for particle (number) transport rather than momentum transport.

items.name: toroidal_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
items.description: Toroidal neon velocity at the plasma boundary is the toroidal component of the density-weighted bulk velocity of neon impurity ions at the last closed flux surface, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It is the density-weighted mean over all neon ion charge states and is local, not a flux-surface average.
items.documentation: Toroidal neon velocity at the plasma boundary is the toroidal component of the density-weighted bulk velocity of neon impurity ions at the last closed flux surface. The toroidal component is taken in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Because no neon ionization state is specified, the elemental neon velocity is the density-weighted mean over all neon ion charge states present at that locus. The component and charge-state aggregation are defined by $$ v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}} = \left(\frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}\,\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}}\right) \cdot \hat{\phi} $$ where $q$ indexes neon ion charge states, $n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}$ is the number density of charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}$ is its bulk velocity, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$. This quantity is a local boundary value and does not imply a flux-surface average, poloidal average, toroidal average, or charge-state sum. The flux-surface-averaged boundary counterpart is toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary; the same toroidal component at other radial loci includes [toroidal_neon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) and [toroidal_neon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier). Sign convention: Positive when the density-weighted neon ion flow is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: electron_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Electron particle transport coefficient relating diffusive flux to the opposing number-density gradient without specifying a spatial direction.
items.documentation: The electron diffusion coefficient characterizes electron particle diffusion through a local Fickian relation between diffusive particle flux and the electron number-density gradient. It does not select a spatial direction or a particular transport mechanism. For a scalar Fickian closure, the defining relation is: $$ \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_e\nabla n_e $$ where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive electron particle flux density, $D_e$ is the electron diffusion coefficient, $n_e$ is the electron number density, and $\nabla$ denotes the spatial gradient. The minus sign expresses down-gradient transport for positive diffusivity. This is an electron-specific [particle diffusivity](name:particle_diffusivity), not an electron energy or momentum transport coefficient. It excludes convective contributions to the electron particle flux and is not a sum of directional diffusion coefficients. The [poloidal electron diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_electron_diffusion_coefficient) is the poloidal-poloidal diagonal specialization within an anisotropic particle-diffusion tensor. The scalar closure above applies when a single coefficient represents the flux-gradient response; the general quantity does not require equal diffusion in all directions or encode off-diagonal tensor couplings.

items.name: toroidal_coordinate_of_reflector
items.description: Toroidal angular coordinate of the center of the sphere defining a reflector’s spherical mirror surface, locating that center around the symmetry axis.
items.documentation: The quantity is the toroidal angle of the center of the sphere that defines a reflector’s spherical mirror surface. It identifies the reflector-center azimuth, not the mirror’s angular extent, orientation, or curvature. The toroidal angle $[?25l\phi_c$ of the sphere center is defined from its projection onto the horizontal plane: $$ \phi_c = \operatorname{atan2}(y_c,x_c) $$ where $x_c$ and $y_c$ are the center coordinates in the right-handed Cartesian basis $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$, with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$. Equivalently, $\phi_c$ is the angular coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. Its geometric meaning parallels [toroidal coordinate of an optical element](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_optical_element), but the locus here is the reflector sphere center. Sign convention: Positive when the angle is measured in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, counter-clockwise when viewed from above along $+\hat{Z}$.

items.name: deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description: Number density of the effective deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the local, intensive particle count per physical volume on the last closed magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation: Number density of the effective deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species at the plasma boundary is the local, intensive particle count per physical volume for that effective species evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the limiting closed magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off-layer region. The local effective deuterium-tritium number density is the zeroth velocity moment of its distribution function at a boundary point: $$ n_{DT}(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \int f_{DT}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v $$ where $n_{DT}$ is the effective deuterium-tritium fuel-pseudo-species number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity of the effective pseudo-species, $f_{DT}$ is its phase-space distribution function, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. This quantity applies to the deuterium-tritium fuel mixture represented as one effective pseudo-species, rather than to separate deuterium and tritium populations. It is a local boundary value with no averaging over the boundary surface or over a volume, and no additional charge-state aggregation is implied by the effective-species representation. It is the deuterium-tritium-specific instance of [density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). Unlike flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary, it denotes the local value at the plasma boundary rather than an average over that last closed magnetic flux surface.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_flux_loop
items.description: Major-radius coordinate of each geometric point defining a flux-loop position, measured as perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation: The quantity is the non-negative major-radius coordinate $R$ of each geometric point defining a flux-loop position. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is the distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. For horizontal Cartesian coordinates $X$ and $Y$ in a right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis whose vertical direction coincides with cylindrical $\hat{Z}$, the coordinate is defined by: $$ R = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2} $$ where $X$ and $Y$ are the point's Cartesian coordinates along $\hat{x}$ and $\hat{y}$, and $R$ is its major-radius coordinate. The quantity applies separately to every geometric point defining one flux-loop position, including a partial loop; it is not a loop-wide average, centroid, or other aggregation of those points. It is a geometric coordinate only and does not represent the loop's other position coordinates, linked magnetic flux, induced voltage, or [effective flux-loop area](name:area_of_flux_loop). This quantity is the flux-loop-specific specialization of the general [radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate): it retains the same major-radius definition while identifying the point as part of flux-loop geometry. The complete point position requires its corresponding toroidal and vertical coordinates.

items.name: perturbed_plasma_mass_density_real_part
items.description: In-phase component of the complex first-order plasma mass-density eigenfunction for one toroidal Fourier harmonic in linear MHD stability theory.
items.documentation: The quantity is the real, in-phase component of the complex first-order plasma mass-density perturbation eigenfunction associated with one toroidal Fourier harmonic in linear MHD stability theory. The complete complex quantity is perturbed plasma mass density. The real component is defined by $$ \widetilde{\rho}_{n,\mathrm{real}}(\mathbf{x}) = \operatorname{Re}\!\left[\widetilde{\rho}_n(\mathbf{x})\right] $$ where $\widetilde{\rho}_n$ is the complex first-order mass-density eigenfunction, $n$ is the toroidal Fourier mode number, and $\mathbf{x}$ denotes position. The decomposition is relative to the phase convention of the complex eigenfunction. This quantity excludes the imaginary quadrature component and must not be interpreted as the magnitude of the complex perturbation. Its meaning parallels the real component of the corresponding temperature eigenfunction, [perturbed plasma temperature real part](name:perturbed_plasma_temperature_real_part).

items.name: thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Local vector rate of angular-momentum transfer to the thermal-ion population per unit volume caused by Coulomb collisions, without restricting orbit class or spatial direction.
items.documentation: Thermal-ion torque density due to collisions is the local vector source of angular momentum transferred to the bulk thermal-ion population by Coulomb collisions with other charged populations. It is the thermal-ion member of the broader [ion torque density due to collisions](name:ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) family. For the selected thermal-ion population, the collisional torque-density vector is defined from its distribution function by $$ \boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{r}) = \int d^3v\,\bigl(\mathbf{r} \times m_i\mathbf{v}\bigr)\,C_{i,\mathrm{coll}}[f_i](\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v}) $$ where $\mathbf{r}$ is position relative to the torque origin, $m_i$ is the ion mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_i$ is the thermal-ion distribution function, and $C_{i,\mathrm{coll}}$ is its Coulomb-collision operator. At parent level, the quantity includes the allowed orbit and spatial-direction contributions; [co-passing thermal-ion torque density due to collisions](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) and [toroidal thermal-ion torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) are corresponding restrictions. It excludes torque deposited in fast-ion populations. Sign convention: Positive when a resolved torque-density component points along the corresponding positive basis vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: helium_3_density_at_pedestal_top
items.description: Helium-3 ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal, summed over all helium-3 ion charge states.
items.documentation: Helium-3 ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the local volumetric abundance of helium-3 ions, including all ionization states. It applies to the helium-3 ion population at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. The charge-state-summed density is defined by $$ n_{^3\mathrm{He}} = \sum_z n_{^3\mathrm{He}^{z+}} $$ where $n_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the local helium-3 ion number density, $n_{^3\mathrm{He}^{z+}}$ is the local number density of helium-3 ions in charge state $z$, and $z$ is the positive integer ion charge state. This quantity is evaluated locally at the pedestal top defined by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). The sum includes all helium-3 ion charge states and excludes neutral helium-3; the quantity is neither a flux-surface average nor a volume average. It is the helium-3 species component of [density at the pedestal top](name:density_at_pedestal_top), whereas [helium-3 density at the limiter](name:helium_3_density_at_limiter) refers to a different spatial locus.

items.name: carbon_density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description: Particle number density of the carbon-ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local carbon-ion count per physical volume, summed over all carbon ion charge states.
items.documentation: Particle number density of the carbon-ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local carbon-ion count per physical volume at that location, summed over all carbon ion charge states. It represents carbon ions specifically, rather than electrons, other ion species, or neutral carbon. The defining relation is $$ n_{\mathrm{C,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{C}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}} $$ where $n_{\mathrm{C,axis}}$ is the carbon-ion number density at the magnetic axis, the subscript $\mathrm{C}$ denotes the carbon-ion population, $N_{\mathrm{C}}$ is the number of carbon ions, $V$ is physical volume, and the subscript axis denotes evaluation at the magnetic axis. The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient vanishes. It applies to the complete carbon-ion population at that location and is summed over all carbon ion charge states; it is neither a flux-surface or volume integral nor a neutral-carbon density. This is the carbon-specific realization of the population-independent [density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It differs from [oxygen density at the magnetic axis](name:oxygen_density_at_magnetic_axis) only in the counted ion species, and from [carbon density at the internal transport barrier](name:carbon_density_at_internal_transport_barrier) in the evaluation locus.

items.name: parallel_gyrocenter_momentum_flux_normalized_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
items.description: Normalized parallel gyrocenter toroidal angular-momentum flux of a gyrokinetic eigenmode due to E×B drift is the rotating-frame spectral contribution from the perturbed electrostatic potential’s E×B drift to the mode’s parallel gyrocenter momentum transport.
items.documentation: Normalized parallel gyrocenter toroidal angular-momentum flux of a gyrokinetic eigenmode due to $E\times B$ drift is the normalized spectral contribution, evaluated in the rotating frame, of the perturbed electrostatic potential's $E\times B$ drift to the parallel gyrocenter part of toroidal angular-momentum flux. The toroidal component is the $\hat{\phi}$ component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The normalization is defined relative to the reference momentum-flux normalization for the same eigenmode: $$ \widehat{\Pi}_{\parallel,\phi}^{E\times B} = \frac{\Pi_{\parallel,\phi}^{E\times B}}{\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}} $$ where $\widehat{\Pi}_{\parallel,\phi}^{E\times B}$ is this normalized contribution, $\Pi_{\parallel,\phi}^{E\times B}$ is the corresponding unnormalized parallel gyrocenter toroidal angular-momentum-flux contribution from the perturbed electrostatic-potential $E\times B$ drift in the rotating frame, $\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reference momentum-flux normalization, $E$ is the perturbed electric field associated with the electrostatic potential, $B$ is the magnetic field, the subscript $\parallel$ denotes the part associated with gyrocenter motion parallel to $B$, and the subscript $\phi$ denotes toroidal angular momentum about the symmetry axis. The quantity applies to one specified linear gyrokinetic eigenmode and to the rotating-frame representation of that mode; it is not summed over eigenmodes, wave-number spectrum, or transport channels. Its aggregation convention is a single-channel normalized eigenmode contribution, not a total turbulent momentum flux. It is the electrostatic-potential $E\times B$ channel in the additive decomposition of the normalized parallel gyrocenter toroidal angular-momentum flux. The perturbed parallel vector-potential channel and the [perturbed parallel magnetic-field channel](name:parallel_gyrocenter_momentum_flux_normalized_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode_due_to_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field) are separate contributions and are excluded from this quantity. Sign convention: Positive when the $E\times B$-drift contribution transports positive parallel gyrocenter toroidal angular momentum across a magnetic flux surface toward increasing flux label, with positive toroidal angular momentum corresponding to the $+\hat{\phi}$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: magnetic_field
items.description: Local total magnetic-induction vector in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius, φ is toroidal angle, and Z is vertical height; it does not select a source contribution, perturbation state, component, magnitude reduction, or evaluation locus.
items.documentation: Local total magnetic-induction vector is the magnetic flux-density vector at a point, carrying both the local field direction and field strength. It is the unqualified parent quantity before selecting a source contribution, perturbation state, component, scalar reduction, spatial aggregation, or evaluation locus. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the vector resolves into radial, toroidal, and vertical components as $$ \mathbf{B} = B_R\hat{\mathbf{R}} + B_\phi\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}} + B_Z\hat{\mathbf{Z}} $$ where $\mathbf{B}$ is this local total magnetic-induction vector; $B_R$ is its radial projection, $B_\phi$ is its [toroidal magnetic-field component](name:toroidal_magnetic_field), and $B_Z$ is its [vertical magnetic-field component](name:vertical_magnetic_field); and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$, $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$, and $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ are the corresponding basis vectors. The frame is right-handed with $\hat{\mathbf{R}} \times \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}} = \hat{\mathbf{Z}}$; $R$ is major radius measured from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counterclockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$, and $Z$ is vertical height. The quantity applies wherever a local magnetic induction is defined, including confined plasma and surrounding vacuum regions, and no particle species or population is selected or aggregated. It is pointwise and vector-valued: it is not the [magnetic field magnitude](name:magnetic_field_magnitude), a flux-surface-average magnetic field, or an extremum such as the [maximum magnetic field](name:maximum_magnetic_field). No cylindrical component, source contribution, perturbation state, or named locus is implied by the unqualified name. When a [magnetic vector potential](name:magnetic_vector_potential) $\mathbf{A}$ is used, $\mathbf{B} = \nabla \times \mathbf{A}$; $\mathbf{A}$ is the magnetic vector potential and $\nabla \times$ is the curl operator, and a gage change affects $\mathbf{A}$ without changing $\mathbf{B}$. Source-qualified fields such as the [vacuum magnetic field](name:vacuum_magnetic_field) and [plasma magnetic field](name:plasma_magnetic_field) are vector contributions of the same kind and add vectorially when they belong to the same electromagnetic state; the [toroidal vacuum magnetic field](name:toroidal_vacuum_magnetic_field) is the toroidal projection of the vacuum contribution. The [reference magnetic field](name:reference_magnetic_field) is a reference total magnetic-induction vector of the same kind, not a source-specific contribution; the [toroidal magnetic field at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_magnetic_field_at_magnetic_axis) is the toroidal projection evaluated at the magnetic-axis locus. Sign convention: Positive when the vacuum toroidal magnetic-field component is directed along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: ion_charge_state_temperature
items.description: Temperature of ions in a specified charge state measures their random translational kinetic energy after bulk flow is removed, rather than their ionization or excitation energy.
items.documentation: Temperature of ions in a specified charge state is an energy-equivalent measure of their random translational motion relative to that population's bulk flow. It characterizes the selected ion population, not its internal electronic energy. For an individual charge state, the defining kinetic relation is $$ T_s = \frac{2}{3}\left\langle E_{\mathrm{rand}}\right\rangle_s $$ where $T_s$ is the energy-equivalent temperature, $s$ identifies the ion species and charge state, $E_{\mathrm{rand}}$ is a particle's translational kinetic energy relative to that population's bulk flow, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_s$ denotes a number-weighted average over particles in that state. The quantity is charge-state-resolved, rather than averaged over all charge states or ion species. When the selected population is a defined charge-state bundle, its temperature is the density-weighted mean over the included charge states, not their sum. The species-level temperature is instead the density-weighted mean over all its charge states. Bulk-flow kinetic energy, ionization energy, and excitation energy are excluded. For a thermal population, this temperature supplies the random kinetic energy per particle entering the [thermal ion charge-state pressure](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_pressure). Unlike [plasma temperature](name:plasma_temperature), it does not combine the electron and ion populations into a single effective thermal state.

items.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_particle_flux
items.description: Poloidal ion charge-state particle flux is the signed net ion crossing rate per unit area normal to the local poloidal direction for one species and ionization state, including thermal and nonthermal ions.
items.documentation: Poloidal ion charge-state particle flux is the signed net number flow of ions of one specified species and ionization charge state per unit area perpendicular to the local poloidal direction. It describes local poloidal particle transport in the edge plasma, including thermal and nonthermal ions. The flux is the poloidal projection of the state's particle-flux vector: $$ \Gamma_{s,q,\mathrm{p}} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s,q}\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}} $$ where $\Gamma_{s,q,\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal particle flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s,q}$ is the net particle-flux vector including thermal and nonthermal contributions, $s$ identifies the ion species, $q$ identifies its ionization charge number, and $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the local poloidal unit vector. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The poloidal unit vector lies in a plane of constant $\phi$ and follows increasing poloidal angle $\theta$; the geometric orientation of that angle must be specified. This is the [ion charge-state particle flux](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux) evaluated through an oriented surface whose normal is the poloidal unit vector. It is local, not surface-integrated or flux-surface-averaged, and it is not summed over charge states. Summing the charge-state contributions for the same species gives the [poloidal ion particle flux](name:poloidal_ion_particle_flux). Unlike [parallel ion charge-state particle flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux), this projection selects a geometric poloidal direction rather than the magnetic-field direction. Sign convention: Positive when the net ion number flow follows increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

items.name: neon_density
items.description: Number density of neon impurity ions, summed over the included ionization states; line-averaged and volume-averaged forms express the same elemental content.
items.documentation: Neon density is the number of neon impurity ions per unit volume, summed over all included charged ionization states. It represents elemental neon content rather than the density of one selected charge state; neutral neon atoms are excluded. $$ n_{\mathrm{Ne}} = \sum_{z \in \mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{Ne}}} n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{z+}} $$ where $n_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the charge-state-summed neon ion density, $n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{z+}}$ is the density of neon ions in charge state $z+$, and $\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the set of included charged ionization states. This species-specific quantity is a member of density. The same charge-state-summed field may be spatially averaged; [volume_averaged_neon_density](name:volume_averaged_neon_density) represents its volume average, while a charge-state-resolved quantity such as [ion_charge_state_density](name:ion_charge_state_density) selects one ionization state and is not equivalent.

items.name: total_ion_particle_source_rate
items.description: Total ion particle source rate is the net ion addition or removal integrated over a plasma volume, summed over all ion species and ionic charge states.
items.documentation: Total ion particle source rate is the net rate of ion production or loss, summed over all ion species and ionic charge states and integrated over a specified plasma volume. Its global value covers the entire plasma volume and supplies the source contribution to the total-ion particle-number balance. The integrated net rate is defined by $$ S_i^{\mathrm{tot}}(V)=\int_V\sum_a\sum_{q\geq 1}\left(S_{a,q}^{+}-S_{a,q}^{-}\right)\,dV $$ where $S_i^{\mathrm{tot}}(V)$ is the total ion particle source rate in the integration region $V$, $a$ indexes ion species, $q$ is the positive ionic charge number, $S_{a,q}^{+}$ and $S_{a,q}^{-}$ are the local volumetric ion production and removal rates for that species and charge state, and $dV$ is a physical volume element. The local rates combine all contributing source and sink processes. Each ion is counted once, without charge weighting; neutral particles are excluded from the ion count. Transitions between included ionic charge states cancel in the total, whereas conversion between neutral and ionized populations changes the ion count. Positive values indicate net ion addition and negative values indicate net removal. This is a particle-number source, not an electric-charge source or the full inventory change, which also includes transport across the integration boundary. This quantity is the species-summed, volume-integrated specialization of [ion particle source rate](name:ion_particle_source_rate). The [cumulative inside-flux-surface total ion particle source rate](name:cumulative_inside_flux_surface_total_ion_particle_source_rate) restricts the integration region to the volume enclosed by a magnetic flux surface; it recovers the global value when that region encompasses the entire plasma volume.

items.name: ratio_of_iron_density_to_electron_density
items.description: Dimensionless abundance ratio of charge-state-summed iron-ion number density to local free-electron number density.
items.documentation: This quantity is the local iron-to-electron abundance ratio in a plasma, comparing the population of iron ions with unbound free electrons. $$ R_{\mathrm{Fe}/e} = \frac{n_{\mathrm{Fe}}}{n_e} $$ where $R_{\mathrm{Fe}/e}$ is the iron-to-electron abundance ratio, $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the total [iron-ion number density](name:iron_density), and $n_e$ is the local [free-electron number density](name:electron_density). The numerator is summed over all positive iron ionization states, while the denominator counts free electrons and excludes electrons bound in atoms, molecules, or ions. This is a local ratio with no volume averaging, maximum operation, or specified spatial locus. The ratio is the iron-specific counterpart of the general [ion-density-to-electron-density ratio](name:ratio_of_ion_density_to_electron_density); its numerator is the charge-state-summed iron density and its denominator is the electron-density parent quantity.

items.name: inverse_of_square_of_major_radius
items.description: Geometric inverse-square-major-radius coefficient for toroidal plasma equilibrium, including flux-surface-averaged forms used in magnetic-geometry relations.
items.documentation: This quantity represents the reciprocal-square major-radius dependence of a geometric coefficient in toroidal plasma equilibrium. It characterizes the metric scaling associated with the distance from the machine symmetry axis. For the direct inverse-square form, the coefficient is defined by $$ K_R = \frac{1}{R^2} $$ where $K_R$ is the inverse-square-major-radius coefficient and $R$ is the major radius in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The quantity applies to toroidal equilibrium geometry and is not the major radius itself or its direct square. It denotes the inverse-square geometric factor; any aggregation over a magnetic flux surface is an additional operation rather than part of the unaggregated quantity. The [flux-surface-averaged inverse-square-major-radius coefficient](name:flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_square_of_major_radius) is the corresponding instance obtained by averaging this inverse-square factor over a magnetic flux surface. The quantity is therefore the reciprocal-square counterpart of [square_of_major_radius](name:square_of_major_radius), with the inverse relationship supplying the geometric scaling.

items.name: fast_neutron_flux_of_toroidal_field_coil
items.description: Incident crossing rate of fast neutrons per unit area on the inboard-facing surface of a toroidal field coil.
items.documentation: Incident crossing rate of fast neutrons per unit area on the inboard-facing surface of a toroidal field coil is the surface density of neutrons whose kinetic energy is at or above the fast-neutron threshold and whose trajectories cross that surface into the coil. The inboard-facing surface is the side of the toroidal field coil facing the toroidal symmetry axis. At a point on that surface, the defining angular-flux integral is: $$ \Phi_\mathrm{fast}^{\mathrm{TF,in}}(\mathbf{x}) = \int_{E_\mathrm{fast}}^\infty \int_{4\pi} \varphi_n(\mathbf{x}, E, \hat{\Omega})\, \max\!\left(0, -\hat{\Omega}\!\cdot\!\hat{\mathbf{n}}_\mathrm{TF,in}(\mathbf{x})\right)\, d\Omega\, dE $$ where $\Phi_\mathrm{fast}^{\mathrm{TF,in}}$ is the fast neutron flux of the toroidal field coil at surface point $\mathbf{x}$, $\mathbf{x}$ is a point on the inboard-facing surface, $E$ is neutron kinetic energy, $E_\mathrm{fast}$ is the fast-neutron threshold, $\hat{\Omega}$ is neutron flight direction, $\varphi_n$ is the angular neutron flux, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_\mathrm{TF,in}$ is the unit normal directed outward from the coil material at the inboard-facing surface, and $d\Omega$ is the solid-angle element. The scope is limited to toroidal field coils and to their inboard-facing surfaces; it does not include correction coils, poloidal field coils, the outboard-facing surface, or a whole-coil combination of surfaces. The quantity is normalized by the receiving surface area and is not the area-integrated neutron rate, cumulative neutron fluence, total neutron production rate, or material response caused by the neutron field. The fast-neutron threshold is an essential part of the convention: neutrons below $E_\mathrm{fast}$ are excluded, and a different threshold defines a different fast-neutron flux. The analogous quantity for a correction coil is [fast neutron flux of correction coil](name:fast_neutron_flux_of_correction_coil); it uses the same incident fast-neutron crossing concept but a different coil population.

items.name: toroidal_coordinate_of_soft_xray_detector
items.description: Toroidal angle of the geometric center of a soft X-ray detector in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation: The quantity is the toroidal coordinate of the geometric center of a soft X-ray detector. The center is the detector geometry reference point, including the center of a circular detector or the origin of its local detector coordinate system. The toroidal angle is defined from the detector-center Cartesian coordinates: $$ \phi_{\rm det} = \operatorname{atan2}(y_{\rm det}, x_{\rm det}) $$ where $x_{\rm det}$ and $y_{\rm det}$ are the Cartesian coordinate values of the detector center in the right-handed $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis, with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$. The corresponding vertical location is given by the [vertical coordinate of the soft X-ray detector](name:vertical_coordinate_of_soft_xray_detector). Sign convention: Positive when the detector center lies in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: fast_particle_pressure
items.description: Fast-particle pressure is the isotropic scalar pressure contribution of the total suprathermal (nonthermal) particle population, combining its field-parallel and transverse stress contributions.
items.documentation: Fast-particle pressure is the scalar kinetic pressure of the total suprathermal (nonthermal) particle population. It represents the isotropic pressure associated with the field-parallel and transverse stresses; the directional stresses themselves need not be equal. For a gyrotropic pressure tensor, the scalar pressure is one-third of its trace: $$ p_{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{p_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) + 2p_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x})}{3} $$ where $p_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is fast-particle pressure, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, $p_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the [parallel fast-particle pressure](name:parallel_fast_particle_pressure), and $p_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the [perpendicular fast-particle pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_particle_pressure), defined per transverse direction. Both components refer to the same population at the same position; the factor of two accounts for the two transverse directions. The quantity applies locally to the full suprathermal population, across all velocities, pitch angles, and orbit classes. Contributions are summed over fast-particle species and all charge states, not averaged. A flux-surface average is a separate spatial aggregation of these local values; the unqualified quantity does not require that average. Fast-particle pressure excludes [thermal plasma pressure](name:thermal_plasma_pressure). It is distinct from a species-specific or charge-state-specific pressure, either directional component, and pressure restricted to an individual orbit class. Restricting the same pressure contribution to orbit classes gives the [co-passing fast-particle pressure](name:co_passing_fast_particle_pressure), [counter-passing fast-particle pressure](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure), and [trapped fast-particle pressure](name:trapped_fast_particle_pressure). Their contributions sum to the full fast-particle pressure when the classes form an exhaustive, nonoverlapping partition of the population.

items.name: perpendicular_trapped_fast_particle_pressure
items.description: Perpendicular trapped fast-particle pressure is the field-perpendicular kinetic-pressure component carried by suprathermal particles on magnetically trapped orbits.
items.documentation: Perpendicular trapped fast-particle pressure is the gyrotropic kinetic-pressure component perpendicular to the local magnetic field, carried by suprathermal particles on magnetically trapped orbits. Trapped particles reverse their field-parallel motion at magnetic mirror points. This is the stress per transverse degree of freedom, not the sum of both transverse stresses or the scalar trace pressure. The local perpendicular pressure is defined by the trapped-population second velocity moment: $$ p_{s,\perp,\mathrm{tr}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_c \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{tr},s,c}(\mathbf{x})} \frac{m_s v_\perp^2}{2} f_{s,c}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v $$ Here, $p_{s,\perp,\mathrm{tr}}$ is the perpendicular trapped fast-particle pressure; $s$ labels the particle species, and $c$ labels its charge state; $m_s$ is the mass of species $s$; $\mathbf{x}$ is position; $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity; $v_\perp$ is the magnitude of the velocity component perpendicular to the local magnetic field; $f_{s,c}$ is the suprathermal distribution for species $s$ and charge state $c$; $\Omega_{\mathrm{tr},s,c}(\mathbf{x})$ is the trapped region of velocity space at that position; and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The factor of one half gives the mean over the two perpendicular velocity directions. Contributions are summed over all charge states of species $s$; distinct species are not summed in this species-specific quantity. The local moment may vary over a magnetic flux surface; its flux-surface average is the average of that same moment over the surface. The population is restricted to suprathermal trapped particles and excludes thermal, co-passing, and counter-passing particles. Perpendicular refers to the magnetic-field direction, not the normal to a flux surface. This is the trapped-orbit contribution to [perpendicular fast-particle pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_particle_pressure), excluding the [perpendicular co-passing fast-particle pressure](name:perpendicular_co_passing_fast_particle_pressure) and [perpendicular counter-passing fast-particle pressure](name:perpendicular_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure). For the same trapped population, the [trapped fast-particle pressure](name:trapped_fast_particle_pressure) is the scalar pressure related to the [parallel trapped fast-particle pressure](name:parallel_trapped_fast_particle_pressure) by $p_{s,\mathrm{tr}}=(p_{s,\parallel,\mathrm{tr}}+2p_{s,\perp,\mathrm{tr}})/3$, where $p_{s,\parallel,\mathrm{tr}}$ is the parallel component and $p_{s,\perp,\mathrm{tr}}$ is this perpendicular component.

items.name: fast_particle_torque_due_to_j_cross_b_force
items.description: Fast-particle torque due to the j×B force is the volume-integrated torque vector acting on the fast-particle population through the magnetic Lorentz force density generated by its current density and the magnetic field.
items.documentation: Fast-particle torque due to the $j \times B$ force is the volume-integrated torque vector acting on the fast-particle population through the magnetic part of the Lorentz force density associated with the fast-particle current density and the magnetic field. It represents angular-momentum transfer to that fast-particle population, not to thermal particles or material structures. The torque vector over a volume $V$ is defined by the moment of the $j \times B$ force density: $$ \boldsymbol{\tau}_{f,j\times B} = \int_V \mathbf{r} \times \left(\mathbf{j}_f \times \mathbf{B}\right)\, dV $$ where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{f,j\times B}$ is the fast-particle torque due to the $j \times B$ force, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the chosen torque origin to the volume element, $\mathbf{j}_f$ is the fast-particle current density, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, and $dV$ is the volume element. This vector parent is distinguished from component-specific projections; [toroidal fast-particle torque due to the $j \times B$ force](name:toroidal_fast_particle_torque_due_to_j_cross_b_force) is the toroidal component of the same fast-particle torque. It excludes torque channels not represented by the fast-particle current-cross-magnetic-field force density. Sign convention: Positive when a reported component of $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{f,j\times B}$ is aligned with the positive direction of its stated projection axis, with vector cross products evaluated by the right-hand rule; in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the toroidal component is positive along $+\hat{\phi}$ toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, counterclockwise when viewed from the $+\hat{Z}$ side.

items.name: length_variation_of_interferometer_beam
items.description: Signed plasma-induced change in the effective optical path accumulated along an interferometer beam relative to its corresponding no-plasma reference path.
items.documentation: This quantity is the signed plasma-induced change in effective optical path length accumulated along an electromagnetic propagation path represented by an interferometer beam. It describes an optical delay or advance caused by the plasma, rather than the unperturbed geometric path length. The variation is defined as $$ \Delta L = L_{\mathrm{plasma}} - L_{\mathrm{ref}} $$ where $\Delta L$ is the optical path-length variation, $L_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the effective optical path along the beam in the presence of plasma, and $L_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the corresponding effective path without plasma. This quantity applies to the net change accumulated along the interferometer beam's complete line of sight. It is a path-integrated optical quantity, not a local path-length density, an unperturbed geometric length, or a separate phase-calibration coefficient. As the variation of [length of an interferometer beam](name:length_of_interferometer_beam), it expresses the plasma-induced departure from the reference path. The associated phase shift provides the optical information used to derive [line-integrated electron number density](name:line_integrated_electron_number_density). Sign convention: Positive when the plasma-affected effective optical path length exceeds the corresponding no-plasma reference path.

items.name: argon_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description: Particle number density of argon ions evaluated on the flux surface assigned to an internal transport barrier, summed over all argon ion charge states and excluding neutral argon.
items.documentation: Particle number density of argon ions evaluated on the flux surface assigned to an internal transport barrier is the local density of the argon-ion population at that flux-surface location. The number density is defined by $$ n = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{\Delta N}{\Delta V} $$ where $n$ is number density, $N$ is the number of counted particles, and $V$ is volume. For argon, the count is summed over all ionic charge states and excludes neutral argon. This species-specific quantity is a member of [density at the internal transport barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier), alongside [boron density at the internal transport barrier](name:boron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier). The internal transport barrier is the designated flux-surface location where reduced cross-field turbulent transport permits steep density gradients.

items.name: perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_energy
items.description: Perpendicular normalized particle perturbed energy is the dimensionless velocity-space moment of a species' perturbed distribution in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, weighted by the perpendicular speed squared times the total speed squared and normalized to the unperturbed total-speed-squared energy moment of the same species.
items.documentation: Perpendicular normalized particle perturbed energy is the perpendicular member of the particle perturbed-energy moment family for a species in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode. Its velocity-space weight is the perpendicular speed squared multiplied by the total speed squared, and the reference normalization is the corresponding unperturbed total-speed-squared energy moment. The quantity is defined as the ratio of the weighted perturbed moment to the unperturbed reference moment: $$ M_{\perp E,s} = \frac{\displaystyle\int \tfrac{1}{2} m_s v_\perp^2 v^2\,\delta f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v}{\displaystyle\int \tfrac{1}{2} m_s v^2\, v^2\, f_{0,s}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v} $$ where $m_s$ is the particle mass of species $s$, $v_\perp$ is the particle speed perpendicular to the local magnetic-field direction, $v_\parallel$ is the particle speed parallel to the local magnetic-field direction, $v^2 = v_\parallel^2 + v_\perp^2$ is the total particle speed squared, $\delta f_s$ is the perturbed particle distribution of the eigenmode, $f_{0,s}$ is the unperturbed (equilibrium) particle distribution, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The denominator is the unperturbed total-speed-squared energy moment shared by the parent [normalized particle perturbed energy](name:normalized_particle_perturbed_energy) and its parallel counterpart, so the parallel and perpendicular members are directly comparable. This scalar is the perpendicular entry of the [normalized particle perturbed energy](name:normalized_particle_perturbed_energy) decomposition and is paired with the parallel normalized particle perturbed energy evaluated with the same perturbed distribution and normalization. It is distinct from the [perpendicular normalized particle perturbed pressure](name:perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure), whose weight is the perpendicular speed squared alone: the energy moment retains the additional total-speed-squared factor. Because a linear eigenmode carries an arbitrary complex amplitude, only comparisons made under the same eigenmode amplitude and phase convention are physically meaningful. Sign convention: Positive when the velocity-space integral of $\tfrac{1}{2} m_s v_\perp^2 v^2\,\delta f_s$ is positive under the chosen eigenmode phase convention.

items.name: oxygen_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description: Number density of oxygen ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the local, intensive particle count per physical volume on the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all charged oxygen ionization states.
items.documentation: Number density of oxygen ions at the plasma boundary is the local, intensive particle count per physical volume for the oxygen-ion population evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the limiting closed magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off-layer region. The local charge-state-summed oxygen ion density at a boundary point is the zeroth velocity moment of the oxygen-ion distribution functions: $$ n_{\mathrm{O}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{z=1}^{8}\int f_{\mathrm{O}^{z+}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v $$ where $n_{\mathrm{O}}$ is the oxygen-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is time, $z$ is the positive oxygen ionization state, $f_{\mathrm{O}^{z+}}$ is the phase-space distribution function for that state, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. This quantity applies specifically to oxygen ions and sums the populations from singly ionized through fully stripped oxygen. It excludes neutral oxygen and other ion species, and it is a local boundary value with no averaging over the boundary surface or over a volume. It is the oxygen-specific instance of [density at the plasma boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The flux-surface-averaged oxygen density at the plasma boundary represents the same charge-state-summed oxygen-ion content averaged over the last closed magnetic flux surface rather than evaluated locally.

items.name: cold_neutral_velocity
items.description: Cold neutral velocity is the line-of-sight component of the bulk flow of low-energy neutral atoms, identified from the Doppler shift of their emission.
items.documentation: Cold neutral velocity is the line-of-sight component of the bulk drift vector of a cold neutral particle population. It represents convective neutral motion after averaging over particle velocities and over the contributing cold-neutral population states. The component is defined from the parent [neutral velocity](name:neutral_velocity) by $$ v_{n,c,ell} = \mathbf{v}_{n,c} \cdot \hat{\ell} $$ where $\mathbf{v}_{n,c}$ is the bulk velocity of the cold neutral population, $\hat{\ell}$ is the selected line-of-sight unit vector, and $v_{n,c,\ell}$ is the signed projected velocity. The projection is the velocity represented by the Doppler centroid of the corresponding cold-neutral emission component. This quantity is distinct from [hot neutral velocity](name:hot_neutral_velocity), which describes the energetic neutral population, and from [neutral internal state velocity](name:neutral_internal_state_velocity), which is resolved for a specified internal state. It excludes thermal speed and velocity spread, which are higher moments of the velocity distribution. Sign convention: Positive when the cold-neutral bulk velocity points along the chosen positive line-of-sight unit vector $\hat{\ell}$.

items.name: y_coordinate_of_sensor_attachment_point
items.description: Signed Cartesian y coordinate of the point where a sensor is mechanically attached to a device component, in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) machine frame with z vertical.
items.documentation: Signed Cartesian $y$ coordinate of the point where a sensor is mechanically attached to a device component is the $\hat{y}$ component of the attachment-point position. The coordinate is defined in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis, with $\hat{z}$ vertical and $(\hat{x}, \hat{y})$ spanning the horizontal plane. The coordinate is the projection of the attachment-point position vector onto the $\hat{y}$ basis direction: $$ y_\mathrm{attach} = \mathbf{r}_\mathrm{attach} \cdot \hat{y} $$ where $y_\mathrm{attach}$ is this signed coordinate, $\mathbf{r}_\mathrm{attach}$ is the position vector of the sensor attachment point relative to the Cartesian frame origin, and $\hat{y}$ is the positive $y$-direction unit basis vector. This quantity applies to the mechanical point where the sensor is attached to a device component. It is not the sensor sensing point, line-of-sight point, active volume position, sensor centroid, or a separate component reference point; no averaging or aggregation over multiple attachment points is implied. Together with [x_coordinate_of_sensor_attachment_point](name:x_coordinate_of_sensor_attachment_point) and [z_coordinate_of_sensor_attachment_point](name:z_coordinate_of_sensor_attachment_point), it specifies the Cartesian position of the same attachment point. This quantity is only the $y$ component and does not include the $x$ or $z$ components. Sign convention: Positive when the attachment point is displaced in the $+\hat{y}$ direction of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis from the frame origin.

items.name: voltage_of_valve
items.description: Voltage applied to a gas-injection valve to drive its opening, serving as the electrical input to the valve's gas-flow response.
items.documentation: Voltage of valve The applied voltage is defined by $$ U = \varphi_{\mathrm{drive}} - \varphi_{\mathrm{ref}} $$ where $U$ is the valve drive voltage, $\varphi_{\mathrm{drive}}$ is the electric potential of the driven terminal, and $\varphi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the electric potential of its circuit reference terminal. The valve response relates this applied signal to the derived [gas flow of the valve](name:gas_flow_of_valve). The voltage is the electrical input to that relationship, not the resulting gas throughput or particle injection rate. Sign convention: Positive when the driven terminal is at higher electric potential than its reference terminal.

items.name: runaway_electron_density
items.description: Number density of runaway electrons, the suprathermal electron population for which electric-field acceleration can overcome collisional drag.
items.documentation: Number density of runaway electron The local density is the zeroth momentum-space moment of the runaway-electron distribution: $$ n_{e,\mathrm{RE}} = \int f_{e,\mathrm{RE}}(\mathbf{p})\,\mathrm{d}^3p $$ where $n_{e,\mathrm{RE}}$ is the runaway-electron number density, $\mathbf{p}$ is electron momentum, and $f_{e,\mathrm{RE}}$ is the runaway-electron momentum distribution at the same spatial position and time. The integral covers all momenta represented in that population. Thermal electrons and suprathermal electrons outside the runaway population are excluded. No orbit-class restriction or spatial averaging is implicit. Unlike [runaway-electron current density](name:runaway_electron_current_density), this quantity counts particles without weighting them by charge and velocity. The [volume-averaged runaway-electron density](name:volume_averaged_runaway_electron_density) is the integral of this local density over the confined plasma volume divided by that volume. The [volume-integrated runaway-electron density](name:volume_integrated_runaway_electron_density) is the integral itself and represents the total runaway-electron count rather than a number density.

items.name: electron_source_rate_due_to_surface_emission
items.description: Instantaneous electron-equivalent source rate supplied by surface emission of material from plasma-facing surfaces, weighted by the electron contribution of each emitted species after ionization.
items.documentation:
Instantaneous electron-equivalent source rate supplied by surface emission is the rate at which ionization of material released from plasma-facing surfaces adds electrons to the plasma particle balance. It aggregates all emitted fuel, molecular, and impurity species over all plasma-facing surfaces, with each emitted particle weighted by the number of bound electrons it can contribute after full ionization. The global rate is defined by integrating the emitted particle flux density over the plasma-facing surface area: $$ S_e^{\mathrm{surf}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{pf}}} \sum_s 
u_{e,s}\,\Gamma_s^{\mathrm{emit}}(\mathbf{x})\,dA $$ where $S_e^{\mathrm{surf}}$ is the electron-equivalent surface-emission source rate, $A_{\mathrm{pf}}$ is the total plasma-facing surface area, $s$ indexes emitted species, $\Gamma_s^{\mathrm{emit}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the emitted particle flux density of species $s$ at surface position $\mathbf{x}$ directed toward the plasma, $dA$ is a surface element, and $
u_{e,s}$ is the electron yield of one emitted particle on full ionization. For an emitted atom, $
u_{e,s}=Z_s$ with $Z_s$ the nuclear charge number; for an emitted molecule or compound particle, $
u_{e,s}$ is the sum of the nuclear charge numbers of its constituent atoms. Surface emission includes recycling, delayed outgassing, and physical or chemical sputtering only insofar as the released material returns toward the plasma and is ionized. This quantity is the electron-specific counterpart of source_rate_due_to_surface_emission, is distinct from externally supplied material represented by [electron_source_rate_due_to_injection](name:electron_source_rate_due_to_injection), excludes electron loss by incidence on surfaces, and contributes to [total_electron_source_rate](name:total_electron_source_rate). Sign convention: Positive when ionization of material emitted from plasma-facing surfaces supplies electron-equivalent particles to the plasma.

items.name: electron_power_at_outer_divertor_target
items.description: Electron power deposited on the outer divertor target by incident electrons, integrated over the wetted strike-zone surface.
items.documentation: Electron power deposited on the outer divertor target by incident electrons integrated over the wetted strike-zone surface is the target-integrated electron energy-transfer rate to the material surface of that target. The outer divertor target is the target on the larger-major-radius side in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The deposited electron power is the surface integral of the local electron energy-flux density directed into the wetted outer-target area: $$ P_{e,\mathrm{outer}} = \int_{A_{w,\mathrm{outer}}} q_{e,\perp}\,dA $$ where $P_{e,\mathrm{outer}}$ is the electron power at the outer divertor target, $A_{w,\mathrm{outer}}$ is the wetted strike-zone area, $dA$ is a target-surface area element, and $q_{e,\perp}$ is the electron energy-flux density directed from the plasma into the target material. This is the electron-channel component of power at the outer divertor target; ion, neutral, radiation, and other non-electron contributions are excluded. It is the outer-target counterpart of [electron power at the inner divertor target](name:electron_power_at_inner_divertor_target).

items.name: thickness_of_iron_core_segment
items.description: Full non-negative toroidal extent of a rectangular iron-core segment between its pair of opposite faces, measured along the toroidal direction φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It is perpendicular to the segment's radial width along R and vertical height along Z.
items.documentation: Full non-negative toroidal extent of a rectangular iron-core segment between its pair of opposite faces, measured along the toroidal direction $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is the major radius from the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is the vertical height. The thickness is the face-to-face separation of paired points on the two opposite toroidal-facing faces along the local toroidal unit vector: $$ t = \left| (\mathbf{x}_+ - \mathbf{x}_-) \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}} \right| $$ where $t$ is the segment thickness in m, $\mathbf{x}_-$ and $\mathbf{x}_+$ are position vectors in m of paired points on the two opposite faces lying on the same line parallel to $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the local toroidal unit vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Together with the [width of the iron-core segment](name:width_of_iron_core_segment), the radial extent along $R$, and the [height of the iron-core segment](name:height_of_iron_core_segment), the vertical extent along $Z$, the thickness completes the mutually orthogonal triplet of extents describing the segment as a rectangular block whose cross section lies in the poloidal $(R, Z)$ plane and is extruded along $\phi$. It excludes any diagonal, chordwise, or arc-length measure across the segment.

items.name: difference_of_neutral_beam_doppler_wavelength_and_reference_wavelength_of_spectral_line
items.description: Signed displacement of a neutral-beam spectral-line wavelength from its reference value, produced by bulk neutral-beam motion along the viewing line of sight.
items.documentation: This quantity is the signed difference between the Doppler-displaced wavelength of a neutral-beam spectral line and its unshifted reference wavelength of the spectral line. It represents the bulk neutral-beam velocity projected along the viewing line of sight. The displacement is defined by $$ \Delta\lambda_{\mathrm{D}} = \lambda_{\mathrm{D}} - \lambda_{\mathrm{ref}} \simeq \lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}\frac{v_{\mathrm{los}}}{c} $$ where $\lambda_{\mathrm{D}}$ is the Doppler-displaced wavelength, $\lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reference wavelength, $v_{\mathrm{los}}$ is the signed bulk velocity component along the line of sight, and $c$ is the speed of light. The approximation applies when the projected velocity is small compared with $c$. The quantity excludes the distinct wavelength displacement produced by the Lorentz shift from the motional Stark electric field; that effect is represented by [difference of fast neutral beam motional Stark wavelength and fast neutral beam reference wavelength of spectral line](name:difference_of_fast_neutral_beam_motional_stark_wavelength_and_fast_neutral_beam_reference_wavelength_of_spectral_line). Sign convention: Positive when the Doppler-displaced wavelength exceeds the reference wavelength, corresponding to a redshift.

items.name: vertical_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux
items.description: Vertical neutral internal-state momentum flux density is the vertical transport rate of vertical linear momentum carried by neutral particles in one specified internal state. It is the vertical-vertical component of the neutral momentum-flux tensor for that state.
items.documentation: The vertical neutral internal-state momentum flux density is the vertical transport component of linear momentum carried by neutral particles restricted to one specified atomic, molecular, charge, or excitation state. It is the $ZZ$ component of the state-resolved momentum-flux tensor, not a particle flux or a local momentum source. For the state-resolved neutral distribution, the vertical component is defined by $$ \Pi_{ZZ}^{(s)} = \hat{Z} \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(s)} \cdot \hat{Z} = \int m_s v_Z^2 f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v $$ where $s$ identifies the internal state, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(s)}$ is its momentum-flux tensor, $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical basis direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $m_s$ is the mass of a neutral particle in state $s$, $v_Z=\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{Z}$ is the vertical velocity component, and $f_s$ is the state-resolved velocity distribution. The vertical direction is the $Z$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; it is not the radial, toroidal, or magnetic-field-parallel direction. As a diagonal $ZZ$ tensor component formed from $v_Z^2$, this quantity is nonnegative for any nonnegative state-resolved velocity distribution. This component is the vertical member of the parent neutral internal-state momentum flux, differs from the [radial](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux), [toroidal](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux), [parallel](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux), and linear internal-state components, and is the state-resolved counterpart of [vertical neutral momentum flux](name:vertical_neutral_momentum_flux).

items.name: accumulated_tritium_count_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Cumulative number of tritium atoms delivered by gas injection since plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count where each tritium atom corresponds to one equivalent electron.
items.documentation: The accumulated tritium count due to gas injection is the running total of tritium ($^3\mathrm{H}$) atoms introduced to the plasma vessel through gas injection valves, accumulated continuously from plasma breakdown onward. The quantity is dimensionless, representing each injected atom as an equivalent-electron contribution scaled by its atomic number. For tritium, whose atomic number is $Z = 1$, the equivalent-electron inventory equals the raw atom count directly: $$ N_\mathrm{eq} = Z \cdot N_\mathrm{atoms} = N_\mathrm{atoms} $$ where $N_\mathrm{atoms}$ is the total number of tritium atoms injected after breakdown. The equivalent-electron convention provides a species-independent basis for comparing injected particle inventories — for higher-$Z$ species such as argon ($Z = 18$), the multiplier is correspondingly larger. This is the time-integrated form of tritium_count_due_to_gas_injection, accumulating monotonically as gas is puffed after breakdown. Tritium introduced before breakdown is tracked separately as tritium_prefill_count. The deuterium analog in the same equivalent-electron framework is [deuterium_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_deuterium_count_due_to_gas_injection).

items.name: vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity
items.description: Mean edge-plasma ion flow along the toroidal symmetry axis, resolved for one specified species and ionization charge state.
items.documentation: The vertical ion charge-state velocity is the projection of the local bulk flow of a specified ion species and ionization charge state onto the vertical direction. It describes directed motion in the edge plasma in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is the vertical component of the [ion charge-state velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity), defined by the first velocity moment: $$ u_{s,q,Z}=\hat{\mathbf z}\cdot\mathbf u_{s,q}=\frac{\int (\mathbf v\cdot\hat{\mathbf z})f_{s,q}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\int f_{s,q}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v} $$ where $u_{s,q,Z}$ is the vertical bulk-flow component, $\mathbf u_{s,q}$ is the bulk velocity vector, $s$ identifies the ion species, $q$ is its ionization charge number, $\mathbf r$ is position, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity, and $f_{s,q}$ is the selected population's phase-space number density. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf z}$ points along the symmetry axis toward increasing $Z$. Both integrals cover particle velocity space; the definition requires nonzero population density. Only the selected ion species and charge-state population contribute; neutral particles and other species are excluded. If a charge-state bundle is specified, its distribution combines the member states, giving their number-density-weighted mean velocity rather than a sum of velocities. This quantity is a signed flow component, not a speed, thermal velocity spread, or particle flux; the vertical direction is not generally the poloidal or magnetic-field-parallel direction. The [vertical ion velocity](name:vertical_ion_velocity) is instead the density-weighted mean of these components over all ionic charge states of the species. Sign convention: Positive when the selected ion population's bulk flow has a component toward increasing $Z$.

items.name: total_absorbed_wave_power
items.description: Total coherent electromagnetic-wave power transferred directly to all plasma particle populations and integrated over all spatial locations.
items.documentation: Total absorbed wave power is the total rate at which coherent electromagnetic waves transfer energy directly to all plasma particle populations, with contributions integrated over the plasma volume. $$ P_{\rm abs} = \left.\frac{dE_{\rm particles}}{dt}\right|_{\rm waves} $$ where $P_{\rm abs}$ is absorbed wave power, $E_{\rm particles}$ is the combined energy of all included plasma particle populations, $t$ is time, and the subscript “waves” restricts the derivative to direct energy transfer from the coherent electromagnetic-wave field. This quantity is globally aggregated: it is summed over all species, charge states, populations, and spatial locations. It includes direct wave-to-particle transfer and excludes electromagnetic power that remains in the wave field and energy subsequently redistributed between particle populations by collisions. It is the species-summed specialization of [absorbed wave power](name:absorbed_wave_power), unlike [electron absorbed wave power](name:electron_absorbed_wave_power), which is restricted to electron populations. It is also the global counterpart of [total absorbed wave power at the inside flux surface](name:total_absorbed_wave_power_at_inside_flux_surface), which retains only the power enclosed within a selected flux surface; Fourier-resolved contributions are represented by [per-toroidal-mode total absorbed wave power](name:per_toroidal_mode_total_absorbed_wave_power).

items.name: per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density
