items.description: Flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate of coherent radio-frequency wave energy absorption by thermal ions of a specified species and charge state, resolved by toroidal Fourier mode number.
items.documentation: Toroidal-mode-resolved thermal-ion charge-state power density is the flux-surface-averaged rate at which coherent radio-frequency waves transfer energy directly to thermal ions of a specified species and charge state per unit physical volume. Each contribution corresponds to one toroidal Fourier harmonic. For a magnetic flux surface, the mode-resolved deposition is defined by $$ p_{a,z}^{(n_\phi)} = \left\langle Q_{a,z}^{(n_\phi)} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}} $$ where $p_{a,z}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the flux-surface-averaged modal power density, $Q_{a,z}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the corresponding local volumetric rate of wave energy transfer to thermal ions, $a$ identifies the ion species, $z$ identifies its charge state, $n_\phi$ is the integer toroidal Fourier mode number, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}$ denotes averaging over that magnetic flux surface. The recipient population is restricted to bulk thermal ions of the selected species and charge state; neither charge states nor toroidal modes are summed. This quantity describes direct wave absorption, not subsequent collisional energy redistribution, a local deposition value before flux-surface averaging, or volume-integrated absorbed power. The [fast-ion counterpart](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density) instead describes absorption by nonthermal ions. Summing over all included toroidal harmonics recovers the flux-surface average of [thermal-ion charge-state power density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density), not its unaveraged local value.

items.name: height_of_hard_xray_detector
items.description: Height of a hard X-ray detector is the full edge-to-edge extent of its rectangular aperture along the second local tangential axis, X2, in the local Cartesian (X1, X2, X3) frame.
items.documentation: Height of hard xray detector It applies to a rectangular detector aperture and denotes a full extent, not a half-extent, signed coordinate, detector location, housing dimension, or extent along the local normal. It is distinct from the extent of a separate channel collimating aperture and from the first local tangential extent, represented by the [first local tangential width](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_hard_xray_detector). For a rectangular detector aperture, this height and the [first local tangential width](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_hard_xray_detector) are its two orthogonal in-plane full dimensions; together they determine the aperture opening area. That area contributes to the [hard X-ray detector etendue](name:etendue_of_hard_xray_detector), which also depends on the accepted solid angle.

items.name: neutral_species_atomic_mass
items.description: Neutral-species atomic mass is the neutral-atom reference mass per atom of a selected elemental or isotopic constituent, including its bound electrons.
items.documentation: Neutral-species atomic mass is the reference mass assigned to one atom of a selected elemental or isotopic constituent of a neutral species. It specifies atomic composition using the neutral reference atom, including its bound electrons. The atomic mass is related to the corresponding relative atomic mass by $$ m = A_{\mathrm r}\,m_{\mathrm u} $$ where $m$ is the constituent's reference atomic mass, $A_{\mathrm r}$ is its relative atomic mass, and $m_{\mathrm u}$ is the atomic mass constant, defined as one twelfth of the rest mass of a free neutral carbon-12 atom in its ground state. The value applies per constituent atom, whether the neutral species is atomic or molecular; it is not the total molecular mass or the mass of the neutral population. It is a physical mass, not the integer nucleon count called the mass number, a mass density, or a mass flow rate. The number of constituent atoms per particle is specified separately by [atomic count](name:atomic_count). This quantity specializes [atomic mass](name:atomic_mass) to constituents of neutral species. Unlike [neutral-beam atomic mass](name:neutral_beam_atomic_mass), its scope is not restricted to atoms in an injected beam.

items.name: current_of_divertor
items.description: Net conventional electric current carried by charged particles into all divertor target surfaces, including signed electron and ion contributions.
items.documentation: The total divertor current is the algebraic conventional current delivered by charged particles crossing the plasma-facing surfaces of the complete divertor assembly. It includes ion and electron contributions and excludes neutral-particle flux and displacement current. The current is defined by $$ I_{\mathrm{div}} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{div}}} \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{ch}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dA = \int_{S_{\mathrm{div}}} \sum_s q_s\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_s \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dA $$ where $I_{\mathrm{div}}$ is the total current in A, $S_{\mathrm{div}}$ is the union of divertor target surfaces, $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{ch}}$ is conventional charged-particle current density in A m$^{-2}$, $q_s$ is the signed charge of species $s$ in C, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_s$ is its particle flux density in m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ points from the plasma toward the material. This assembly-integrated quantity differs from [current at a divertor target](name:current_at_divertor_target), which applies to one target, and [current of a divertor tile](name:current_of_divertor_tile), which applies to an individual tile. Sign convention: Positive when conventional charged-particle current flows from the plasma into the divertor material.

items.name: radius_of_detector
items.description: Radius from the center to the circumferential edge of a detector's circular front face, defining its geometric size for optical throughput.
items.documentation: The detector radius is the geometric distance from the center of a circular detector front face to its circumferential edge. The corresponding circular face area is defined by $$ A_{\rm det} = \pi r_{\rm det}^{2} $$ where $A_{\rm det}$ is the detector front-face area, $r_{\rm det}$ is the detector radius, and $\pi$ is the mathematical constant. This quantity applies only when the detector front face has circular geometry. It describes the detector face itself and does not represent a collimating aperture, a filter opening, or a width parameter for a noncircular detector geometry. The face area determined by this radius contributes to the geometric optical throughput represented by [spectrometer etendue](name:etendue_of_spectrometer); it is distinct from the radius of a separate [spectrometer aperture](name:radius_of_aperture).

items.name: electron_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer
items.description: Radial e-folding decay length of the electron heat flux in the scrape-off layer, defined by the inverse magnitude of its outward logarithmic gradient.
items.documentation: The electron heat decay length in the scrape-off layer (SOL) is the radial distance over which the electron heat-flux profile falls to $1/e$ of its separatrix value. It characterizes the spatial scale of electron heat exhaust across the open-field-line region and specializes the channel-unspecified [heat decay length](name:heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer). The decay length is defined as the inverse magnitude of the outward logarithmic gradient of the electron heat flux: $$ \lambda_{q,e} = \left| \frac{\partial \ln q_e}{\partial r} \right|^{-1} $$ where $q_e$ is the electron heat flux and $r$ is radial distance measured outward from the separatrix into the SOL. This quantity includes only the electron heat channel and is distinct from the corresponding [ion heat decay length](name:ion_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer). As the magnitude of a logarithmic gradient, the decay length is non-negative.

items.name: electron_temperature_at_pellet_path
items.description: Background-plasma electron temperature evaluated locally along the pellet’s ablation trajectory, describing the thermal state encountered by the pellet during transit.
items.documentation: The quantity is the local energy-equivalent temperature of background plasma electrons at positions along the pellet trajectory. It describes the plasma encountered by the pellet, not the thermal state of pellet material or an average over the entire trajectory. For an isotropic electron population, the energy-equivalent temperature is defined by $$ T_e = \frac{2}{3}\langle E_e\rangle $$ where $T_e$ is the electron temperature expressed as an energy, and $\langle E_e\rangle$ is the mean random kinetic energy per electron. The quantity applies only to background electrons and is evaluated locally along the pellet path; it is not charge-state aggregated, path-averaged, or a pellet ablation rate. The corresponding [electron density at the pellet path](name:electron_density_at_pellet_path) describes the local free-electron population at the same trajectory locations, while this quantity specifies its thermal energy state.

items.name: maximum_of_back_surface_neutron_flux
items.description: Maximum neutron energy flux escaping through the rear surface of a breeding blanket module toward vessel structures.
items.documentation: This quantity is the greatest local neutron energy flux crossing outward through the rear surface of one breeding blanket module. It measures the escaping neutron load relevant to attenuation toward vessel structures. The maximum is defined from the local back-surface neutron energy flux as $$ q_{n,\max} = \max_{\mathbf{x}\in S_{\mathrm{back}}} q_n(\mathbf{x}) $$ where $q_n(\mathbf{x})$ is the local neutron energy flux at surface position $\mathbf{x}$, and $S_{\mathrm{back}}$ is the rear surface of the module. The quantity applies to fusion neutrons from all included neutron energies, fusion reaction channels, and reacting populations, aggregated into a single local energy-flux value before taking the maximum over the rear surface of one module. It represents neutrons escaping outward from the module and excludes a surface-integrated module power and neutron flux incident on the module's front surface. It is the maximum-over-surface transformation of [back-surface neutron flux](name:back_surface_neutron_flux), which describes the local value without selecting its maximum. It is distinct from [incident neutron power of a breeder blanket module](name:incident_neutron_power_of_breeder_blanket_module), which is the total neutron power arriving at the module, and from [nuclear heating power of a breeder blanket module](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket_module), which describes energy deposited by neutron interactions within the module.

items.name: forward_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
items.description: Forward power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the incident radio-frequency power arriving at its back from the source through the feed line.
items.documentation: Forward power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna denotes the incident radio-frequency traveling-wave power arriving at the back of the antenna through its feed line. It is the source-to-antenna component at the antenna reference plane, before reflected power is subtracted. For a single antenna, the power components referred to the same reference plane satisfy $$ P_{\mathrm{fwd}} = P_{\mathrm{launched}} + P_{\mathrm{ref}} $$ where $P_{\mathrm{fwd}}$ is the forward incident power, $P_{\mathrm{launched}}$ is the net [launched power](name:launched_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), and $P_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the [reflected power](name:reflected_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) returning toward the source. This quantity applies to one ion-cyclotron heating antenna, not a sum over an antenna set. It includes only the forward-traveling component, excluding the backward-traveling reflected component. Subtracting reflected power gives net launched power; forward power is neither this net quantity nor the power subsequently absorbed by the plasma.

items.name: toroidal_argon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description: Signed toroidal bulk-flow velocity of argon ions, density-weighted over charge states and evaluated at the radial location of an internal transport barrier.
items.documentation: The quantity is the density-weighted mean bulk-flow velocity of all argon ion charge states at the radial location assigned to the internal transport barrier. Neutral argon is excluded, and the value is not a volume average over the barrier or surrounding plasma. For argon charge states indexed by $q$, the velocity is defined by $$ v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}} $$ where $n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}$ is the number density of charge state $q$ and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}$ is its bulk-flow component along the toroidal unit vector. The toroidal direction is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $\phi$ increasing toroidally. The charge-state aggregation is the same as for [toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier). Sign convention: Positive when the argon-ion bulk flow points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: parallel_peak_launched_refractive_index_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
items.description: Peak value of the parallel refractive index in the lower-hybrid wave spectrum launched by an antenna. It is the signed value at the dominant spectral peak set by the measured phase difference between neighboring waveguide rows, not an algebraic maximum over all launched components.
items.documentation: Peak value of the parallel refractive index in the lower-hybrid wave spectrum launched by an antenna is the signed parallel refractive-index coordinate of the dominant launched spectral peak. The parallel direction is taken along the local magnetic-field direction at the launcher aperture. The defining value is the refractive index associated with the peak parallel wave number of the launched spectrum: $$ N_{\parallel,\mathrm{peak}} = \frac{c\,k_{\parallel,\mathrm{peak}}}{\omega} $$ where $N_{\parallel,\mathrm{peak}}$ is the peak launched parallel refractive index, $c$ is the speed of light, $k_{\parallel,\mathrm{peak}}$ is the parallel wave number at the dominant peak of the launched lower-hybrid spectrum, and $\omega$ is the wave angular frequency. For this quantity, the dominant peak is the main spectral peak inferred from the measured phase difference between neighboring waveguide rows, through the row-to-row phase advance per projected row separation in the parallel phasing direction. This quantity is not the algebraic maximum of $N_\parallel$ over all launched components; if the main spectral peak lies at negative $N_\parallel$, the peak value is negative.

items.name: lithium_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description: Local number density of lithium ions at the internal transport barrier reference radius, where reduced cross-field transport can produce steep impurity density gradients.
items.documentation: Lithium density at an internal transport barrier is the local number density of lithium ions on the flux surface selected as the barrier reference location. Unless a charge state is specified separately, it represents the elemental lithium ion concentration summed over all ionization states, consistent with the broader [density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier) family. The quantity is the sum of charge-state-resolved contributions evaluated at the ITB reference coordinate $\rho_\mathrm{ITB}$: $$ n_\mathrm{Li}(\rho_\mathrm{ITB}) = \sum_{k=1}^{3} n_{\mathrm{Li}^{k+}}(\rho_\mathrm{ITB}) $$ where $k$ indexes the lithium ionization states (Li$^{1+}$, Li$^{2+}$, Li$^{3+}$) and $\rho_\mathrm{ITB}$ is the normalized radial coordinate of the barrier. Lithium (atomic number $Z = 3$) enters fusion plasmas through pellet injection, evaporation from lithium-coated plasma-facing components, or deliberate wall conditioning. As a low-Z impurity it contributes less radiative cooling than high-Z species, but significant concentrations at the ITB can dilute the fuel ion population. The local value at the barrier is inferred from charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy or from inversion of line-integrated visible or soft-X-ray emission measurements. The corresponding toroidal flow of lithium ions at the same barrier location is given by [toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier), and the lithium density adjacent to plasma-facing components is separately described by [lithium_density_at_limiter](name:lithium_density_at_limiter).

items.name: power_due_to_synchrotron_radiation
items.description: Total electromagnetic power emitted by relativistic electrons as synchrotron radiation while their gyromotion is curved by the plasma magnetic field.
items.documentation: Power due to synchrotron radiation is the total electromagnetic power emitted by relativistic electrons as synchrotron radiation while their gyromotion is curved by the plasma magnetic field. It is a mechanism-specific contribution to the plasma radiative power and refers to emitted radiation, not stored electromagnetic energy. For an emitting plasma volume $V$, the quantity is defined by the volume integral of the local synchrotron volumetric emissivity: $$ P_{\mathrm{syn}} = \int_V p_{\mathrm{syn}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV $$ where $P_{\mathrm{syn}}$ is the power due to synchrotron radiation, $p_{\mathrm{syn}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local synchrotron volumetric emissivity formed from the relativistic electron phase-space distribution and the local magnetic field, $\mathbf{x}$ denotes position, and $dV$ is a volume element. This quantity includes only synchrotron emission and excludes [bremsstrahlung power](name:bremsstrahlung_power) and [power due to line radiation](name:power_due_to_line_radiation). It denotes gross electromagnetic power emitted by the radiating electrons and is distinct from net synchrotron power escaping a plasma-facing or material boundary after reabsorption or reflection.

items.name: perpendicular_co_passing_fast_particle_pressure
items.description: Flux-surface-averaged transverse kinetic stress of nonthermal particles on untrapped orbits whose orbit-averaged toroidal motion follows the plasma current.
items.documentation: The perpendicular co-passing fast-particle pressure is the flux-surface-averaged field-perpendicular component of the kinetic stress of a represented nonthermal particle species. Co-passing particles occupy untrapped guiding-center orbits with orbit-averaged toroidal motion in the plasma-current direction. The component is defined by the transverse second moment of the co-passing fast-particle distribution: $$ p_{s,\perp,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}(\psi)=\left\langle\int_{\mathcal{C}_s(\mathbf{x})}\frac{m_s v_\perp^2}{2}\,f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v\right\rangle_\psi $$ where $p_{s,\perp,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}$ is the perpendicular co-passing fast-particle pressure, $s$ labels the represented species, $\psi$ labels a magnetic flux surface, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathcal{C}_s(\mathbf{x})$ is the velocity-space subset belonging to co-passing orbits at that position, $m_s$ is the particle mass, $f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle distribution function, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The squared transverse speed is $v_\perp^2=|\mathbf{v}-(\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{b})\hat{b}|^2$, where $\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$. The factor of one-half gives the mean stress in the two field-perpendicular directions. The brackets denote a normalized magnetic-flux-surface average with weight proportional to $dS/|\nabla\psi|$, where $dS$ is the surface-area element and $\nabla\psi$ is the spatial gradient of the flux label. Thus the quantity is a surface average, not a local stress at one point. Only the co-passing nonthermal population contributes; thermal, trapped, and counter-passing particles are excluded. Multiple fast-particle populations of the represented species contribute additively, not through a density-weighted mean; no all-species or all-charge-state total is implied. Particle velocities are used without subtracting the mean flow, so perpendicular directed-motion stress is retained. Together with the [parallel co-passing fast-particle pressure](name:parallel_co_passing_fast_particle_pressure), this component determines the [co-passing fast-particle pressure](name:co_passing_fast_particle_pressure) through $p_{s,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}=(p_{s,\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}+2p_{s,\perp,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}})/3$, where $p_{s,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}$ is one-third of the kinetic-stress trace and $p_{s,\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}$ is the corresponding field-parallel component, with the same population restriction and flux-surface averaging.

items.name: toroidal_halo_current
items.description: Toroidal component of the electric current carried by halo plasma on open magnetic field lines between the last closed flux surface and first wall during a disruption.
items.documentation: Toroidal halo current is the toroidal component of the electric-current vector carried by halo plasma on open magnetic field lines between the last closed flux surface and the first wall during a disruption. It is the toroidal member of the vector quantity [halo current](name:halo_current). The component is defined by $$ I_{\phi} = \mathbf{I}_{\mathrm{halo}} \cdot \hat{\phi} $$ where $\mathbf{I}_{\mathrm{halo}}$ is the integrated halo-current vector and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Unlike [poloidal halo current](name:poloidal_halo_current), this component measures current along the direction of increasing toroidal angle and excludes the poloidal component. Sign convention: Positive when the halo current flows in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part
items.description: In-phase radial fluid-velocity component obtained from the real part of a complex linear-MHD perturbation eigenfunction for a specified toroidal Fourier mode.
items.documentation: This quantity is the signed, in-phase radial component of the complex first-order plasma-velocity eigenfunction. It is the real-part component of [radial perturbed plasma velocity](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity), not the velocity magnitude or its imaginary quadrature component. $$ v_{r,\mathrm{Re}}(R,Z;n)=\operatorname{Re}\!\left[\tilde{\mathbf{v}}_1(R,Z;n)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{R}}\right] $$ Here $\tilde{\mathbf{v}}_1$ is the complex perturbed plasma-velocity eigenfunction, $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the radial unit vector, $R$ is major radius, $Z$ is vertical height, and $n$ is the toroidal Fourier mode number, all expressed in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The real part depends on the selected eigenmode phase and normalization. Sign convention: Positive when the radial perturbation velocity points toward increasing major radius $R$.

items.name: vertical_neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description: Dimensionless vertical momentum flux-limiter coefficient that scales the free-streaming upper bound on neutral-particle momentum-flux density in edge-plasma transport closures.
items.documentation: The vertical neutral momentum flux-limiter coefficient is the vertical component of the neutral-particle specialization of the general momentum flux-limiter coefficient vector, providing the dimensionless limiter factor for neutral momentum transport along the vertical $Z$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame in multi-fluid edge-plasma models. It bounds the vertical neutral momentum-flux density by the free-streaming limit when the neutral mean free path is large relative to macroscopic gradient scales. The vertical component $\alpha_Z$ is defined as the ratio of the magnitude of the modeled vertical neutral momentum-flux density to its positive free-streaming upper bound: $$ \alpha_Z = \frac{|\Pi_Z|}{\Pi_Z^{\rm free}}, \qquad \Pi_Z^{\rm free} = m_n n_n \left(u_Z^{\rm free}\right)^2 $$ where $\Pi_Z$ is the modeled vertical neutral momentum-flux density component along $\hat{Z}$, $\Pi_Z^{\rm free}$ is the corresponding free-streaming upper bound, $m_n$ is the neutral particle mass, $n_n$ is the neutral number density, and $u_Z^{\rm free}$ is the nonnegative free-streaming reference speed for neutral motion along $\hat{Z}$. The constraint $\alpha_Z \in [0, 1]$ makes the coefficient a magnitude limiter; any sign of the vertical momentum flux is carried by $\Pi_Z$, not by $\alpha_Z$. This quantity is the vertical member of the [neutral momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) vector and is distinct from the [parallel neutral momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), which is taken along the magnetic-field direction, and the toroidal neutral momentum flux-limiter coefficient, which is taken along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It is a limiter coefficient, not the neutral momentum-flux density itself.

items.name: power_of_divertor_due_to_convection
items.description: Power deposited on all divertor targets by convective plasma particle flux, comprising thermal enthalpy and directed kinetic energy carried by streaming ions and electrons from the scrape-off layer.
items.documentation: Convective power at all divertor targets quantifies the energy transported to those targets by plasma particles streaming from the scrape-off layer. It comprises thermal enthalpy and directed kinetic-energy contributions carried by convective plasma particle flux into the material surfaces, summed over all divertor targets. The all-target convective divertor power is the sum of the incident convective energy flux over the wetted surfaces of the divertor targets: $$ P_{\mathrm{conv,div}} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{D}} \int_{A_k} \sum_s \Gamma_{s,k}^{\mathrm{in}} \left(h_{s,k} + \frac{1}{2} m_s |\mathbf{u}_{s,k}|^2\right) \, dA $$ where $\mathcal{D}$ is the set of divertor target surfaces, $A_k$ is the wetted surface of target $k$, $dA$ is a surface-area element, and $s$ labels incident species in the convective channel, including streaming ion and electron species. $\Gamma_{s,k}^{\mathrm{in}}$ is the particle-flux density into the material, defined by the positive-into-target surface-normal projection $n_{s,k}\max(\mathbf{u}_{s,k}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}_{\mathrm{in},k},0)$; $n_{s,k}$ is the particle density, $\hat{\mathbf n}_{\mathrm{in},k}$ is the surface normal directed from the plasma into the target, $h_{s,k}$ is the thermal enthalpy per particle, $m_s$ is the particle mass, and $\mathbf{u}_{s,k}$ is the directed flow velocity of the incident particles. This quantity is the all-divertor-target realization of [convective power](name:power_due_to_convection); the corresponding single-target quantity is [convective power at a single divertor target](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_convection), and the broader plasma-facing-surface counterpart is [convective power at plasma-facing wall and divertor surfaces](name:power_at_wall_due_to_convection). It excludes [conductive divertor power](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_conduction), radiative deposition, and [recombination-related divertor plasma power](name:plasma_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination), which are separate channels of the divertor power balance.

items.name: coolant_absorbed_power_of_calorimetry_component
items.description: Thermal power removed from a calorimetry component by its coolant, determined from the coolant enthalpy increase between inlet and outlet.
items.documentation: This quantity is the instantaneous thermal power transferred from one calorimetry component into its coolant. It is specific to the named component and represents coolant-mediated heat extraction rather than a group-wide or plant-wide power total. The enthalpy-balance definition is $$ P_{\mathrm{cool,abs}} = \dot{m}_{c}\left(h_{\mathrm{out}} - h_{\mathrm{in}}\right) $$ where $P_{\mathrm{cool,abs}}$ is the coolant-absorbed thermal power, $\dot{m}_{c}$ is the coolant mass flow rate, and $h_{\mathrm{in}}$ and $h_{\mathrm{out}}$ are the coolant specific enthalpies at the component inlet and outlet states. The enthalpy difference is evaluated from the corresponding coolant thermodynamic states, including the inlet and outlet temperatures. The quantity excludes heat transferred by channels other than the coolant and does not denote accumulated energy. Its time integral from pulse start is the [accumulated coolant-absorbed energy of the calorimetry component](name:accumulated_coolant_absorbed_energy_of_calorimetry_component), while this quantity remains the instantaneous component-level extraction rate. The coolant inlet state is related to the [coolant temperature at inlet](name:coolant_temperature_at_inlet).

items.name: vertical_outline_of_plasma_facing_component
items.description: The vertical coordinate of each point on a plasma-facing component boundary outline is the signed height in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation: The vertical outline coordinate is the signed height $Z$ of each boundary-contour point belonging to a plasma-facing component. It describes the component boundary in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. For outline point $i$, the coordinate is defined by $$ Z_i = \mathbf{r}_i \cdot \hat{\mathbf{Z}} $$ where $Z_i$ is the vertical coordinate of point $i$, $\mathbf{r}_i$ is that point's position vector relative to the cylindrical coordinate origin, and $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the unit vector in the vertical direction. The quantity applies pointwise to one component boundary outline and is not an average, extremum, centroid coordinate, or integrated geometric measure. A closed outline does not repeat its first point as a closing point. This coordinate has the same geometric meaning as the corresponding outline coordinate for a limiter tile or divertor tile, such as [vertical outline of limiter tile](name:vertical_outline_of_limiter_tile) and [vertical outline of divertor tile](name:vertical_outline_of_divertor_tile), but its locus is the plasma-facing component boundary in general. Sign convention: Positive when $Z_i$ increases in the $+\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: calibration_polarization_angle_of_optical_element
items.description: Calibration polarization angle of an optical element is the signed angle from a reference transverse polarization direction to the element's selected polarization axis, viewed along its line of sight toward the plasma.
items.documentation: Calibration polarization angle of an optical element is the orientation angle of the polarization-selective axis of that element in the plane perpendicular to its line of sight. It identifies the electric-field component selected by the element relative to a defined transverse reference direction. The signed angle is defined by $$ \alpha_\mathrm{cal} = \operatorname{atan2}\!\left[-\hat{\ell}\cdot\left(\hat{e}_\mathrm{ref}\times\hat{e}_\mathrm{sel}\right),\ \hat{e}_\mathrm{ref}\cdot\hat{e}_\mathrm{sel}\right] $$ where $\hat{\ell}$ is the line-of-sight unit vector directed from the optical element toward the plasma, $\hat{e}_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference polarization unit vector in the plane normal to $\hat{\ell}$, and $\hat{e}_\mathrm{sel}$ is the selected polarization-axis unit vector in the same transverse plane. This quantity is an axis-alignment calibration parameter, not a measure of polarization ellipticity, polarization purity, or the handedness of a full polarization state. Sign convention: Positive when the selected polarization axis is rotated counter-clockwise from the reference transverse polarization direction as seen looking from the optical element toward the plasma along the line of sight.

items.name: radial_conductivity
items.description: Local electrical response coefficient relating a major-radius electric field to the conductive current density it drives along the cylindrical major-radius direction.
items.documentation: Radial conductivity is the major-radius–major-radius projection of the local plasma electrical-conductivity tensor in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius measured from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; the radial direction points toward increasing $R$. The defining tensor projection is $$ \sigma_{RR} = \hat{R} \cdot \boldsymbol{\sigma} \cdot \hat{R} $$ where $\sigma_{RR}$ is radial conductivity, $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ is the [plasma electrical-conductivity tensor](name:plasma_electrical_conductivity), and $\hat{R}$ is the unit vector in the major-radius direction. For an electric field directed solely along the major-radius direction, the conductive response satisfies $j_R^{\mathrm{cond}} = \sigma_{RR} E_R$, where $j_R^{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the major-radius component of conductive current density and $E_R$ is the major-radius electric-field component. For a general electric field, off-diagonal tensor components can also contribute to the major-radius current density. This is a local plasma transport coefficient, not a spatial average or integrated conductance. Its projection direction is geometric: it is not defined by a minor-radius flux label, a flux-surface normal, or the magnetic-field direction. In contrast, [parallel conductivity](name:parallel_conductivity) projects the same electrical response along the local magnetic field.

items.name: normal_coordinate_of_correction_coil
items.description: Signed coordinate of a correction-coil conductor cross-section outline vertex along the normal axis of the local Frenet-Serret frame, measured from the conductor centerline.
items.documentation: Signed coordinate of a correction-coil conductor cross-section outline vertex along the normal axis of the local Frenet-Serret frame, measured from the conductor centerline, is the scalar projection of the displacement from the centerline point to that vertex onto the local normal direction. The local frame is the right-handed Frenet-Serret frame $(\hat{\mathbf{t}}, \hat{\mathbf{n}}, \hat{\mathbf{b}})$ attached to the correction-coil conductor centerline, with $\hat{\mathbf{b}} = \hat{\mathbf{t}} \times \hat{\mathbf{n}}$. The coordinate is defined by $$ q_n = \left(\mathbf{x}_v - \mathbf{x}_c(s)\right) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}(s) $$ where $q_n$ is the signed normal coordinate of the outline vertex, $\mathbf{x}_v$ is the position vector of the outline vertex, $\mathbf{x}_c(s)$ is the position vector of the conductor centerline at centerline parameter $s$, $s$ identifies the corresponding location along the conductor centerline, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}(s)$ is the normal basis vector of the local Frenet-Serret frame. The scope is the local cross-sectional boundary of a correction-coil conductor; each value refers to one outline vertex at one centerline location and describes only its normal-axis displacement in the local $(\hat{\mathbf{n}}, \hat{\mathbf{b}})$ cross-section plane. It excludes the binormal coordinate, any coordinate of the conductor centerline itself, and any projection along a magnetic-flux-surface normal. The paired [binormal coordinate of a correction coil](name:binormal_coordinate_of_correction_coil) gives the complementary component of the same outline vertex in the local $(\hat{\mathbf{n}}, \hat{\mathbf{b}})$ cross-section plane. Together, the paired outline coordinates define the boundary whose enclosed [cross-sectional area of the correction coil](name:area_of_correction_coil) is a related geometric property. The [normal coordinate of a toroidal-field coil](name:normal_coordinate_of_toroidal_field_coil) has the same local-coordinate meaning for a different coil class. Sign convention: Positive when the displacement from the correction-coil conductor centerline to the outline vertex has a component in the $+\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ direction of the local Frenet-Serret frame.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_strike_point
items.description: Vertical coordinate of a selected divertor strike point, giving its signed height relative to the origin in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation: Vertical coordinate of a selected divertor strike point specifies its signed height relative to the coordinate origin in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height along the toroidal symmetry axis. $$ Z_{\mathrm{s}} = \mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{s}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}} $$ where $Z_{\mathrm{s}}$ is the strike-point vertical coordinate, $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{s}}$ is the position vector of that point relative to the coordinate origin, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along the positive vertical direction. The value applies to one identified strike point. Inner and outer strike points have separate values; no averaging or summation over them is implied. The generic quantity does not select a particular strike-point branch. This coordinate specifies a different geometric location from the [vertical coordinate of an X-point](name:vertical_coordinate_of_x_point). It also differs from the [vertical coordinate of the divertor-target center](name:z_coordinate_of_divertor_target), which locates the target's geometric center rather than the selected strike point. Sign convention: Positive when the displacement from the coordinate origin to the strike point has a positive projection onto the positive vertical direction $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$. The point where a divertor separatrix branch intersects a plasma-facing target. Where $\psi(R_{\mathrm{s}}, Z_{\mathrm{s}}) = \psi_{\mathrm{X}}$, $R_{\mathrm{s}}, Z_{\mathrm{s}}$ is the point on the target surface; $\psi_{\mathrm{X}}$ is poloidal magnetic flux at the primary X-point.

items.name: voltage_of_mass_spectrometer
items.description: Mass-spectrometer detector bias voltage is the signed detector-bias potential difference between the detector electrode or electron-multiplying stage and its bias reference. It is a device-level setting; voltage_of_mass_spectrometer_channel denotes a channel-specific detector bias.
items.documentation: Mass-spectrometer detector bias voltage is the signed detector-bias potential difference applied between the detector electrode or electron-multiplying stage and its bias reference. It is a device-level electrical setting that affects ion collection efficiency or electron-multiplier gain. The detector-bias potential difference is defined by the detector and reference electric potentials: $$ V_\mathrm{bias} = \Phi_\mathrm{det} - \Phi_\mathrm{ref} $$ where $V_\mathrm{bias}$ is the detector bias voltage of the mass spectrometer, $\Phi_\mathrm{det}$ is the electric potential of the detector electrode or electron-multiplying stage, and $\Phi_\mathrm{ref}$ is the electric potential of its bias reference. This quantity applies to the mass spectrometer as a device-level detector bias common to the instrument or defined independently of channel selection. It excludes channel-specific detector biases, which are represented by [mass-spectrometer channel detector bias voltage](name:voltage_of_mass_spectrometer_channel). This quantity is distinct from [mass-spectrometer channel ion current](name:ion_current_of_mass_spectrometer_channel): the ion current is the electrical current associated with collected ions in a channel, whereas the detector bias voltage is the applied potential difference that can affect collection efficiency or gain. Sign convention: Positive when the detector electrode or electron-multiplying stage is at higher electric potential than its bias reference.

items.name: volume_averaged_helium_4_density
items.description: Volume-averaged number density of helium-4 ions over the confined plasma volume, providing a global measure of fusion-ash concentration in deuterium-tritium plasmas.
items.documentation: The volume-averaged helium-4 ion number density quantifies the mean concentration of fusion-ash ions throughout the confined plasma volume. It is the global counterpart of the local [helium-4 ion density](name:helium_4_density) and is distinct from the chord mean [line-averaged helium-4 density](name:line_averaged_helium_4_density). The volume average is defined by $$ \overline{n}_{{}^4\mathrm{He}} = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{r})\,d^3\mathbf{r} $$ where $n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local helium-4 ion number density in m$^{-3}$, $V_p$ is the confined plasma volume in m$^3$, and $\mathbf{r}$ denotes position. The helium-4 ion population is summed over all ionic charge states, while neutral helium is excluded. Its ratio to the volume-averaged electron density is defined by [ratio of volume-averaged helium-4 density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_4_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

items.name: co_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Collisional co-passing torque density for fast ions is the local vector rate of angular-momentum transfer to or from the co-passing fast-ion population caused by Coulomb collisions with background plasma species.
items.documentation: Collisional co-passing torque density for fast ions is the local source density of angular momentum transferred to or from the co-passing fast-ion population by Coulomb collisions. It retains the full torque-density vector for fast ions on the co-passing orbit branch rather than selecting a particular component. The local defining relation is: $$ \boldsymbol{\tau}_{f,\mathrm{co},\mathrm{coll}} = \left.\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{\ell}_{f,\mathrm{co}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{coll}} $$ where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{f,\mathrm{co},\mathrm{coll}}$ is the co-passing fast-ion collisional torque-density vector, $\boldsymbol{\ell}_{f,\mathrm{co}}$ is the co-passing fast-ion angular-momentum density, and $t$ is time; the subscript $\mathrm{coll}$ selects the Coulomb-collisional contribution. This quantity is restricted to the co-passing fast-ion population; it is not the all-orbit [fast-ion torque density due to collisions](name:fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) and is not an aggregate over counter-passing or trapped fast ions. The [toroidal co-passing fast-ion torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_co_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) is the toroidal component-resolved instance of this vector quantity, and this quantity is distinct from collisional energy-transfer density. Sign convention: Positive when a resolved vector component points along its positive basis direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: power_of_plant_system
items.description: Real electrical power assigned at a plant-system boundary, representing absorbed load, net generation balance, or an aggregate of included system loads.
items.documentation: Real electrical power is the rate of electrical-energy transfer or accounting associated with a plant system at its electrical boundary. It excludes reactive power and other non-electrical energy flows. The instantaneous power is defined by $$ P = \frac{\mathrm{d}E}{\mathrm{d}t} $$ where $E$ is the electrical energy associated with the accounting boundary and $t$ is time. The accounting convention is fixed by the specialized quantity. Absorbed power of a plant system represents one-way incoming electrical load, net power of a plant system represents generation minus internal consumption and is positive for net export, and total power of a plant system is the sum of the loads of all included systems. These forms are distinct applications of the same plant-boundary electrical-power concept.

items.name: height_of_correction_coil
items.description: Full non-negative extent of a rectangular correction-coil conductor cross-section measured along the local Frenet–Serret binormal.
items.documentation: The correction-coil height is the full external-envelope dimension of its rectangular conductor cross-section along the binormal direction of the local Frenet–Serret frame $(\hat{\mathbf t}, \hat{\mathbf n}, \hat{\mathbf b})$. It is distinct from the transverse dimension measured along the local normal direction, defined by the [width of a correction coil](name:width_of_correction_coil). $$ h = b_{\max} - b_{\min} $$ where $h$ is the conductor height and $b_{\max}$ and $b_{\min}$ are the signed binormal coordinates of the opposing outer faces, consistent with the [binormal coordinate of a correction coil](name:binormal_coordinate_of_correction_coil). The quantity is the full extent, not a half-height, centerline offset, or cross-sectional area.

items.name: normalized_perturbed_parallel_gyrocenter_current_density_bessel_1
items.description: Dimensionless first-Bessel-weighted parallel current-density moment of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution, capturing its field-aligned finite-Larmor-radius response.
items.documentation: This quantity is the first-order Bessel-weighted, field-parallel current-density moment of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution. It represents the electromagnetic response of a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode in the gyrocenter description. The normalized moment is defined by $$ j_{parallel,J_1}^{\mathrm{norm}} = \frac{q}{j_{\mathrm{ref}}} \int v_{\parallel} J_1(k_{\perp}\rho)\,\delta f_{\mathrm{gc}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v $$ where $j_{\parallel,J_1}^{\mathrm{norm}}$ is the normalized Bessel-weighted parallel current-density moment, $q$ is the charge of the represented particle species, $j_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference current-density scale, $v_{\parallel}$ is the velocity component along the local equilibrium magnetic field, $J_1$ is the first-order Bessel function of the first kind, $k_{\perp}$ is the perpendicular wave-number magnitude, $\rho$ is the particle gyroradius, $\delta f_{\mathrm{gc}}(\mathbf{v})$ is the perturbed gyrocenter distribution function, $\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space coordinate, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The quantity is restricted to the perturbed gyrocenter distribution, the field-parallel velocity channel, and the first-order Bessel weighting. Its aggregation convention is the charge-weighted moment shown in the integral; it is not an unweighted density moment, a perpendicular current channel, an equilibrium contribution, or a particle-frame moment. It is the normalized, parallel specialization of the vector [normalized gyrocenter perturbed current density](name:normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density), with the additional $J_1$ finite-Larmor-radius weighting. Removing that weighting gives the corresponding [parallel normalized gyrocenter perturbed current density](name:parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density). Sign convention: Positive when the charge-weighted perturbed current is directed along the local equilibrium magnetic field, whose orientation is expressed in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: counter_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Counter-passing thermal-ion torque density due to collisions is the local angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume delivered to bulk thermal ions by Coulomb collisions.
items.documentation: Counter-passing thermal-ion torque density due to collisions is the local torque per unit volume transferred to the bulk thermal ion population by Coulomb collisions with contributing charged-particle populations. It is restricted to the counter-passing particle component while retaining the full torque-vector quantity rather than a single axis component. The collisional torque density is related to the collisional force density by $$ \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}} $$ where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the torque density transferred to thermal ions, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the axis about which torque is resolved, and $\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the force density transferred to thermal ions by collisions. This quantity is the counter-passing contribution to [thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions); collision partners and channels are included in the collisional transfer, while other orbit classes are excluded. Its toroidal component is represented by [toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions), while [toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) provides the corresponding toroidal component aggregated over contributing orbit classes. Sign convention: Positive when a resolved torque component points along its corresponding positive basis direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination
items.description: Total power deposited on all divertor target surfaces by recombination processes, comprising both the plasma-ion and neutral-particle recombination channels summed over the full divertor assembly.
items.documentation: Total divertor recombination power is the combined rate at which recombination processes at or near the target surfaces of the divertor assembly release energy into the material, integrated over all targets. It is the divertor-surface counterpart of the volumetric [power_due_to_recombination](name:power_due_to_recombination) and unifies two physically distinct deposition channels: $$ P_\mathrm{rec,div} = P_\mathrm{rec,div}^\mathrm{plasma} + P_\mathrm{rec,div}^\mathrm{neutral} $$ where $P_\mathrm{rec,div}^\mathrm{plasma}$ is [plasma_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination](name:plasma_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination), the energy deposited when plasma ions recombine or neutralize at the material surface, and $P_\mathrm{rec,div}^\mathrm{neutral}$ is [neutral_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination](name:neutral_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination), the energy carried by neutral particles undergoing recombination reactions at the plasma-material interface. This quantity is computed in edge-plasma codes that track ion and neutral fluxes to the targets and apply sheath-energy coefficients along with recombination cross-sections to determine surface deposition. It represents one component of the total divertor heat load alongside conducted, convected, and radiative contributions, and becomes a more prominent fraction of that load in detached or partially detached divertor regimes where volumetric recombination upstream suppresses the ion current reaching the targets.

items.name: thickness_of_breeder_blanket_layer
items.description: Non-negative geometric separation between the inner and outer material interfaces of a breeder blanket layer along the specified thickness direction.
items.documentation: Non-negative geometric separation between the inner and outer material interfaces of a breeder blanket layer is the local through-thickness of that layer along the specified thickness direction. The quantity applies to a single material or functional layer within the blanket, not to the total breeder blanket module build. The layer thickness is defined by the separation of the two bounding interfaces along the thickness coordinate: $$ d_\ell = \left|s_{\ell,\mathrm{out}} - s_{\ell,\mathrm{in}}\right| $$ where $d_\ell$ is the layer thickness in m, and $s_{\ell,\mathrm{in}}$ and $s_{\ell,\mathrm{out}}$ are the signed coordinates in m of the inner and outer layer interfaces along the specified thickness direction. It is not the toroidal width, poloidal height, surface extent, or volume-equivalent thickness of the layer. It is distinct from module-level quantities such as thickness_of_breeder_blanket_module, [lower_thickness_of_breeder_blanket_module](name:lower_thickness_of_breeder_blanket_module), and [upper_thickness_of_breeder_blanket_module](name:upper_thickness_of_breeder_blanket_module). For a radially stacked layer, the thickness direction is the cylindrical $\hat{R}$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

items.name: perpendicular_refractive_index
items.description: Magnitude of the electromagnetic wave vector perpendicular to the local background magnetic field, normalized by the vacuum wave number at the same frequency.
items.documentation: The perpendicular refractive index is the magnitude of the component of the [refractive-index vector](name:refractive_index) perpendicular to the local background magnetic field. It describes the field-transverse part of electromagnetic phase propagation. Its defining relation is $$ n_\perp = \left|\mathbf{n} - (\mathbf{n}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}})\hat{\mathbf{b}}\right| = \frac{k_\perp}{k_0} $$ where $n_\perp$ is the perpendicular refractive index, $\mathbf{n}$ is the refractive-index vector, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector along the local background magnetic field, $k_\perp$ is the [perpendicular wave-vector magnitude](name:perpendicular_wave_vector_magnitude), and $k_0$ is the vacuum wave number at the same wave frequency. Vertical bars denote the Euclidean vector magnitude. This quantity is evaluated locally along a beam or ray path, rather than averaged or integrated along that path, and is not restricted to electron cyclotron emission. It is nonnegative and retains no direction within the perpendicular plane; it is therefore distinct from a signed projection onto a specified transverse axis. For a real phase-gradient vector, $|\mathbf{n}|^2 = n_\parallel^2 + n_\perp^2$, where $n_\parallel$ is the signed [parallel refractive index](name:parallel_refractive_index). The two quantities resolve the parent vector's magnitude relative to the magnetic-field direction.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_flux_loop
items.description: Vertical Z coordinate of a position point associated with one flux loop in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation: The quantity is the vertical coordinate $Z$ of a position point associated with one flux loop. It locates that point along the vertical direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Here $Z$ denotes vertical height, $R$ denotes major radius from the symmetry axis, and $\phi$ denotes toroidal angle. The value applies to an individual position point of a single flux loop; it is not a loop-area quantity, magnetic flux, voltage, or an aggregate over turns, points, or multiple loops. No population or plasma-region restriction is implied. Together with the corresponding radial and toroidal position coordinates, this coordinate locates the flux-loop point in space. It is the flux-loop-specific counterpart of the [vertical coordinate of a measurement position](name:vertical_coordinate_of_measurement_position), which applies the same geometric concept to a generic measurement location. Sign convention: Positive when the flux-loop position lies in the +Z direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description: Number density of hydrogen ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all hydrogen ion charge states.
items.documentation: Number density of hydrogen ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle count per physical volume for the hydrogen-ion population on the last closed magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. The defining zeroth velocity-space moment is $$ n_H(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\int f_H(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v} $$ where $n_H$ is the hydrogen-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_H$ is the hydrogen-ion velocity distribution function, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element. This quantity is evaluated locally at the plasma boundary and is summed over the included hydrogen ion charge states. It excludes neutral hydrogen and is distinct from electron density and from the total ion population represented by ion_density_at_plasma_boundary. The corresponding surface-averaged quantity, flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary, applies the same hydrogen-ion population to an average over the boundary surface rather than a local evaluation. The subject-unspecified parent [density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary) defines the common boundary-density concept, while this quantity fixes the population as hydrogen ions.

items.name: total_absorbed_wave_power_at_inside_flux_surface
items.description: Cumulative power transferred from electromagnetic waves to electrons, ions, and fast populations within a selected magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation: Cumulative absorbed electromagnetic-wave power deposited in the plasma volume enclosed by a selected magnetic flux surface. It includes absorption by electron, ion, and fast populations and represents an enclosed quantity rather than a local power density. The defining relation is $$ P_{\mathrm{abs}}(\psi) = \int_{V(\psi)} p_{\mathrm{abs}}^{\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV $$ where $P_{\mathrm{abs}}(\psi)$ is the cumulative absorbed wave power, $\psi$ is the label of the selected magnetic flux surface, $V(\psi)$ is the volume enclosed by that surface, $p_{\mathrm{abs}}^{\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the total absorbed wave power density at spatial position $\mathbf{x}$ summed over electrons, ions, and fast populations, and $dV$ is the differential volume element. This quantity is cumulative over the enclosed volume and is not a local deposition density or a population-resolved contribution. Population-specific quantities such as [thermal electron power at an inside flux surface](name:thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface) and [thermal ion power at an inside flux surface](name:thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface) resolve components of this aggregate. When the selected surface encloses the full absorbing plasma volume, it equals [total absorbed wave power](name:total_absorbed_wave_power).

items.name: counter_passing_thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Flux-surface-averaged rate of Coulomb-collisional energy transfer per unit volume from counter-passing nonthermal particles to bulk thermal electrons.
items.documentation: Counter-passing thermal-electron collisional power density is the signed volumetric rate of kinetic-energy transfer from counter-passing nonthermal particles to bulk thermal electrons, averaged over a magnetic flux surface. Counter-passing particles follow untrapped guiding-center trajectories whose transit is opposite to the reference co-passing direction. The transfer is defined by the thermal-electron kinetic-energy moment of the Coulomb collision operator: $$ P_{e,\mathrm{counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\psi) = \left\langle \sum_a \int \frac{1}{2}m_e v^2 C_{ea}[f_e^{\mathrm{th}},f_{a,\mathrm{counter}}] \, d^3v \right\rangle_\psi $$ where $P_{e,\mathrm{counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the flux-surface-averaged power density transferred to thermal electrons, $\psi$ labels the magnetic flux surface, $a$ indexes the represented nonthermal donor species, $m_e$ is the electron mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, and $v=|\mathbf{v}|$ is electron speed. The distribution $f_e^{\mathrm{th}}$ describes bulk thermal electrons, $f_{a,\mathrm{counter}}$ is the counter-passing part of the nonthermal distribution of species $a$, and $C_{ea}$ gives the collisional time derivative of the thermal-electron distribution caused by that donor population. The integral covers all electron velocities; the angle brackets denote the physical-volume-weighted average over an infinitesimal shell between neighboring flux surfaces. The orbit restriction applies to the nonthermal donors, not to the receiving thermal electrons. The donor contributions are summed over the represented nonthermal species. Energy transferred to ions or fast electrons, contributions from co-passing or trapped donors, and noncollisional heating are excluded. This quantity describes energy gained by thermal electrons rather than energy gained by the counter-passing donors; the corresponding donor energy exchange has the opposite sign. After applying the same flux-surface average to each contribution, adding the [co-passing thermal-electron contribution](name:co_passing_thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions) and the [trapped thermal-electron contribution](name:trapped_thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions) recovers the flux-surface average of [thermal-electron collisional power density](name:thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions), which includes all represented donor orbit classes. Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions with counter-passing nonthermal particles transfer net kinetic energy to bulk thermal electrons.

items.name: toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_pedestal_top
items.description: Toroidal component of the helium-3 ion fluid velocity at the pedestal top, resolved along the toroidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It is the density-weighted mean over all helium-3 ion charge states and is signed positive for flow toward increasing φ.
items.documentation: Toroidal component of the helium-3 ion fluid velocity at the pedestal top is the helium-3 ion bulk-flow component resolved along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. For species-level helium-3, this intensive quantity is the density-weighted mean over all helium-3 ion charge states at the pedestal top. The charge-state-aggregated toroidal component is defined by $$ v_{\phi,\,^3\mathrm{He}}^{\mathrm{ped}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{^3\mathrm{He}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}\left(\mathbf{v}_{^3\mathrm{He}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}} \cdot \hat{\phi}\right)}{\sum_q n_{^3\mathrm{He}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}} $$ where $q$ indexes helium-3 ion charge state, $n_{^3\mathrm{He}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the number density of that charge state at the pedestal top, $\mathbf{v}_{^3\mathrm{He}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}$ is its ion fluid velocity there, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$. This quantity excludes radial and vertical components in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, vector speed, arithmetic averages over charge states, and values at other loci such as the [magnetic axis](name:toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_magnetic_axis). It is defined where the total helium-3 ion density in the averaging denominator is nonzero. Sign convention: Positive when the helium-3 ion fluid velocity is directed toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_soft_xray_detector
items.description: Signed coordinate of a soft X-ray detector outline vertex along the first local tangential (X1) axis of the detector-local two-dimensional Cartesian frame.
items.documentation: The first local tangential coordinate specifies the signed displacement of an outline vertex along the first tangential axis (X1) of the detector-local Cartesian frame. Together with [second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_soft_xray_detector](name:second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_soft_xray_detector), it defines the polygonal boundary of the soft X-ray detector's sensitive area projected onto the object-local plane. The two coordinates $(X_1, X_2)$ form a right-handed pair intrinsic to the owning detector object; their orientation is fixed per detector installation and is not in general aligned with the machine cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Sign convention: Positive when the vertex displacement is in the direction of the positive first local tangential axis of the detector-local frame.

items.name: bremsstrahlung_power
items.description: Total electromagnetic power emitted by free-free bremsstrahlung as electrons accelerate in the Coulomb fields of plasma ions.
items.documentation: Bremsstrahlung power is the total electromagnetic power emitted by free-free radiation from electron acceleration in the Coulomb fields of plasma ions. It is integrated over the emitting plasma volume and the full photon-frequency range. $$ P_{\mathrm{brem}} = \int_V \int_0^\infty \varepsilon_{\mathrm{brem}}(\mathbf{x},\omega)\,d\omega\,d^3\mathbf{x} $$ where $P_{\mathrm{brem}}$ is the total bremsstrahlung power, $V$ is the emitting plasma volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\omega$ is photon angular frequency, and $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{brem}}$ is the spectral volumetric bremsstrahlung emissivity. This quantity is a contribution to [total plasma radiated power](name:total_plasma_radiated_power) and excludes discrete [line radiation](name:power_due_to_line_radiation) and [synchrotron radiation](name:power_due_to_synchrotron_radiation).

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude
items.description: Flux-surface average of the squared magnitude of the total equilibrium magnetic field, providing a geometric coefficient for equilibrium and neoclassical transport relations.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the surface-averaged squared strength of the total magnetic field on a nested magnetic flux surface. It is a geometric metric coefficient used in equilibrium descriptions and in bounce-averaged and neoclassical transport relations. The flux-surface average is defined by $$ \left\langle B^2 ightangle_\psi =  rac{\displaystyle\oint_{S(\psi)}  rac{B^2}{\lvert
abla\psivert}\,dS}{\displaystyle\oint_{S(\psi)}  rac{1}{\lvert
abla\psivert}\,dS} $$ where $B^2$ is the [square of the magnetic-field magnitude](name:square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude), $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic-flux label of the surface, $S(\psi)$ is the closed magnetic flux surface with that label, $
abla\psi$ is the gradient of the flux label, and $dS$ is the surface-area element. The quantity applies to the total equilibrium magnetic field, including all of its components, and is aggregated over each closed flux surface with the inverse-$\lvert
abla\psivert$ weighting shown above. It is not the pointwise value of $B^2$, the square of a flux-surface-averaged magnetic-field magnitude, or a single magnetic-field component. It is the flux-surface-averaged form of [square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude](name:square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude). It differs from [flux_surface_averaged_magnetic_field_magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_magnetic_field_magnitude), which averages the field magnitude before squaring, and from [flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude), which averages its reciprocal.

items.name: toroidal_reference_magnetic_field
items.description: Toroidal reference magnetic field is the signed toroidal component of the equilibrium magnetic field at the reference point whose major radius is the reference major radius, expressed in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation: Toroidal reference magnetic field is the signed toroidal component of the equilibrium magnetic field at a specified reference point in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The reference point has major radius equal to the [reference major radius](name:reference_major_radius). The defining projection is: $$ B_{\phi,\mathrm{ref}} = \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{eq}}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{ref}}) \cdot \hat{\phi}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{ref}}) $$ where $B_{\phi,\mathrm{ref}}$ is the toroidal reference magnetic field, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equilibrium magnetic field, $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{ref}}=(R_{\mathrm{ref}},\phi_{\mathrm{ref}},Z_{\mathrm{ref}})$ is the full reference point in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reference major radius, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing $\phi$. For an axisymmetric equilibrium, the value is independent of $\phi_{\mathrm{ref}}$. This quantity is the reference-location specialization of [toroidal magnetic field](name:toroidal_magnetic_field). It is distinct from [toroidal magnetic field at magnetic axis](name:toroidal_magnetic_field_at_magnetic_axis), from the magnetic-field magnitude, and from [toroidal vacuum magnetic field](name:toroidal_vacuum_magnetic_field). Sign convention: Positive when $B_\phi$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: iron_density
items.description: Total number density of iron impurity ions in the plasma, summed over all ionization states from singly to fully ionized iron (atomic number Z = 26).
items.documentation: Iron density is the total number density of iron ions present in the plasma, aggregated over all charge states from Fe$^{1+}$ through Fe$^{26+}$ (atomic number $Z = 26$). It characterizes the iron impurity content without resolving the per-charge-state distribution, and may refer to a local point value or a spatially averaged quantity depending on the sampling convention. The total iron ion number density $n_\mathrm{Fe}$ is defined as: $$ n_\mathrm{Fe} = \sum_{z=1}^{26} n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}} $$ where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}$ is the number density of iron in charge state $z$. Iron enters confined plasmas primarily through physical sputtering of high-$Z$ plasma-facing components. Spectroscopic measurements in the vacuum-ultraviolet and soft X-ray ranges resolve individual charge-state emission lines; the total iron density is reconstructed by summing ionization-state-resolved densities derived from ionization balance calculations. This general quantity is concretized by spatial-sampling variants: flux_surface_averaged_iron_density averages the local density over a magnetic flux surface, [line_averaged_iron_density](name:line_averaged_iron_density) represents a chord-integrated value divided by path length, and [volume_averaged_iron_density](name:volume_averaged_iron_density) integrates over the full plasma volume. Position-specific forms are available at key radial locations such as [iron_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:iron_density_at_magnetic_axis), iron_density_at_pedestal, and [iron_density_at_limiter](name:iron_density_at_limiter).

items.name: toroidal_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description: Dimensionless coefficient that scales the collisionless free-streaming upper bound on toroidal momentum-flux density in multi-fluid edge plasma transport closures, capping the flux magnitude while leaving its sign direction unchanged.
items.documentation: In multi-fluid edge plasma transport models, gradient-driven diffusive closures can produce toroidal momentum-flux densities that exceed the physically realizable collisionless free-streaming limit in steep-gradient regions. A toroidal momentum-flux-limiter coefficient $\alpha_{m,\phi}$ is introduced to bound the effective $\hat{\phi}$-projected momentum-flux density, where $m$ denotes momentum and $\phi$ denotes the toroidal projection. The toroidal projection is along $\hat{\phi}$, the tangent to increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ and $\hat{R} \times \hat{\phi} = \hat{Z}$. The bounded toroidal momentum-flux density satisfies the limiter constraint: $$ |\Pi_{\phi}^{\mathrm{lim}}| \le \alpha_{m,\phi}\,\Pi_{\phi}^{\mathrm{FS}} $$ where $\Pi_{\phi}^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the limited toroidal momentum-flux density, $\Pi_{\phi}^{\mathrm{FS}}$ is the toroidal free-streaming momentum-flux reference scale, and $\alpha_{m,\phi}$ is the toroidal momentum-flux-limiter coefficient. This coefficient is the toroidal directional specialization of [momentum-flux-limiter coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), not a particle-, heat-, or energy-flux limiter and not the momentum-flux density itself. It is intrinsically non-negative: it caps the magnitude of the modeled toroidal momentum-flux density and does not carry the positive or negative sign of that flux. Directional siblings include the poloidal, radial, [parallel](name:parallel_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), and [diamagnetic](name:diamagnetic_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) momentum-flux-limiter coefficients.

items.name: poloidal_angle_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe
items.description: Signed poloidal tilt angle of a toroidal magnetic-field probe’s sensitive-axis normal in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, measured clockwise from +R.
items.documentation: The quantity is the signed orientation angle of the normal defining a toroidal magnetic-field probe’s sensitive axis. It specifies the probe’s tilt in the poloidal cross-section, rather than the spatial angle of the probe center. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, let $n_R$ and $n_Z$ denote the components of the probe’s oriented sensitive-axis normal along the increasing-$R$ and increasing-$Z$ directions. The poloidal angle $\theta_{\rm pol}$ is defined by: $$ \theta_{\rm pol} = \operatorname{atan2}(-n_Z,n_R) $$ where $\operatorname{atan2}$ is the two-argument arctangent that preserves the quadrant of the projected normal. The scope is one toroidal magnetic-field probe and its oriented sensitive-axis normal. This is a geometric sensor-orientation quantity, not the poloidal coordinate of the probe center, the direction of the measured magnetic field, or a plasma flux-surface coordinate; it has no plasma-population or region aggregation and is not summed over probes or coil windings. It is a probe-specific application of the parent [poloidal angle](name:poloidal_angle_of_flux_surface): the parent defines the geometric angular measure, while this quantity applies it to the probe’s oriented normal. The complementary [toroidal_angle_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe](name:toroidal_angle_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe) describes the toroidal orientation of the same probe normal, whereas [poloidal_angle_of_measurement_position](name:poloidal_angle_of_measurement_position) describes the angular location of a measurement point. Sign convention: Positive when the sensitive-axis normal points from the outward radial direction toward decreasing $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, following the clockwise direction in the poloidal plane.

items.name: power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating
items.description: Net radiofrequency power absorbed by the plasma through electron cyclotron heating, with source aggregation determined by scope and excluding launched or reflected power.
items.documentation: Electron-cyclotron heating power is the rate at which electron-cyclotron-range electromagnetic waves transfer energy to the plasma, principally through resonant electron absorption. It denotes deposited plasma heating power rather than generator, launched, transmitted, or reflected power. The absorbed power is defined by the volume integral of the local electron-cyclotron heating density: $$ P_{\mathrm{EC}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}} Q_{\mathrm{EC}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV $$ where $P_{\mathrm{EC}}$ is the absorbed power, $Q_{\mathrm{EC}}$ is the local power-transfer density, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the plasma volume. Source aggregation is scope-dependent; the [total electron-cyclotron heating power](name:total_power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating) sums the contributions from all electron-cyclotron wave sources. The quantity is non-negative for net absorption and is distinct from [electron absorbed wave power](name:electron_absorbed_wave_power) when that quantity includes wave absorption without restricting the mechanism to electron cyclotron heating.

items.name: ion_energy_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description: Multiplicative factor setting the maximum permitted ion energy flux relative to a collisionless free-streaming reference while preserving the direction assigned by the transport closure.
items.documentation: The ion energy flux limiter coefficient scales the collisionless free-streaming upper bound on energy flux density carried by a specified ion population. It limits the permitted flux magnitude without choosing or reversing its direction. The limiting relation is: $$ \left|\mathbf{Q}_i\right| \leq f_i Q_{i,\mathrm{fs}} $$ where $\mathbf{Q}_i$ is the limited ion energy flux density, $f_i$ is the ion energy flux limiter coefficient, and $Q_{i,\mathrm{fs}}$ is the nonnegative collisionless free-streaming reference magnitude for the same ion population. The subscript $i$ identifies that population. The coefficient is nonnegative; the free-streaming reference and the transition between unlimited and limited flux are specified by the transport closure. This is the ion-population specialization of the [energy flux limiter coefficient](name:energy_flux_limiter_coefficient), with no particular spatial direction or plasma region prescribed. It applies to species-resolved or aggregated ion energy closures, rather than necessarily denoting a total over all ions. The [total ion energy flux limiter coefficient](name:total_ion_energy_flux_limiter_coefficient) specializes this definition to energy summed over all ion species; the limiter coefficient itself is not a sum of species coefficients. The [ion-state energy flux limiter coefficient](name:ion_state_energy_flux_limiter_coefficient) restricts the closure to a specified ion charge state. This coefficient limits energy transport, not particle or momentum transport. It is neither an energy diffusion coefficient nor the fraction of the free-streaming reference actually carried by the flux.

items.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_velocity_due_to_convection
items.description: Effective velocity for convective transport of thermal energy carried by a specified ion charge state.
items.documentation: This quantity is the effective velocity associated with convective transport of thermal energy carried by a specified ion charge state. It characterizes energy transport rather than the transport of particles alone. $$ v_{E,\mathrm{conv}}^{(s)} = \frac{q_{E,\mathrm{conv}}^{(s)}}{w_{\mathrm{th}}^{(s)}} $$ where $v_{E,\mathrm{conv}}^{(s)}$ is the effective energy-convection velocity, $q_{E,\mathrm{conv}}^{(s)}$ is the convective thermal-energy flux associated with charge state $s$, and $w_{\mathrm{th}}^{(s)}$ is the corresponding thermal-energy density. The ratio is an energy-transport weighting and need not equal the [ion charge-state particle convection velocity](name:ion_charge_state_particle_convection_velocity). It is the thermal effective specialization of [ion charge-state energy velocity due to convection](name:ion_charge_state_energy_velocity_due_to_convection), including the more specific [effective thermal ion charge-state energy velocity due to convection](name:effective_thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_velocity_due_to_convection).

items.name: nuclear_heating_power_of_limiter_tile
